items.spec:
Builds `ui-demos/loadout-eva/index.html`, a standalone maximalist-retro-futurist redesign of LOADOUT.CFG (Evangelion instrumentation DNA, structural grammar only, no branding), replacing the shipped 11-block flat layout as the study to review. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, matching every other ui-demos study; links `../_shared/kp.css` + `../_shared/system.css` + the Silkscreen/VT323/IBM-Plex-Mono Google Fonts stack; `body{overflow:auto;display:block;height:auto;min-height:100%;padding:40px 16px 60px;}`; a bottom-right `.rig` panel with 4 rows (CRT, HUE, VIEWPORT, RUN STATE). Root frame keeps the `.term`/`.term-bar`/`.term-body` naming every standalone study uses (not `.kp-fw*`, which only applies once the desktop embeds a study in an iframe), 3px solid var(--ch) border, the shared 9px/26px drop-shadow filter, solid-ink title bar reading LOADOUT.CFG with the standard 3-glyph decorative cluster. All catalog numbers/descriptions are read verbatim from kit.ts/patch-cells.ts/save.ts at two fixed RUN STATE snapshots (see runState below); no new sentence-shaped copy is introduced (see owedCopy).

Headline structural decisions, expanded in the fields below: (1) the bench-rig schematic plate (loadout-plate-*.png) is CUT entirely, not shrunk. (2) the bench feed (loadout-feed-*.png) survives as a small 'LIVE MONITOR' bezel built by CROPPING the native 304x227 image inside a smaller overflow:hidden viewport (zero resampling, dither-safe), not by scaling it down, so the art-budget-NONE constraint costs zero new art. (3) the pouch's 4-line prose paragraph is CUT to a one-line chip plus the verbatim shipped pointer sentence, justified because DIVE.EXE (duel.tsx:785,937, teaching moment patch-cell-use) and SOLDER.BAY already teach the placement cost and sourcing facts verbatim; cutting it here creates no teaching gap. (4) SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND become a three-panel trinity, each an instrument bay with one huge hero numeral, the single biggest text on the page (extreme scale contrast), staggered in a shallow asymmetric V rather than a tidy 3-up row, framed with a thin hairline border plus new heavier corner brackets instead of the system's usual solid box border. (5) type sizing uses CSS container query units (cqi), not vw: the window's own tile width is what should drive its type scale on a tiled multi-window desktop, not the outer browser viewport, which is the deeper fix for problem 3 (a vw-based clamp would still break because two differently-sized tiled windows at the same browser width would wrongly get the same type scale).

fluid.unitStrategy: Container query units (cqi, 1cqi = 1% of the nearest ancestor's inline-size with container-type:inline-size set), NOT vw, for every clamp(). Rationale: a KP/OS window's own tile width, not the outer browser viewport, is what should drive its type scale on a tiled multi-window desktop; vw-based clamps would leave the root cause of problem 3 unfixed (two differently-sized tiled windows at the same browser width would still wrongly share a type scale).
containers: `.lo-eva` (wraps the whole content area inside `.term-body`): container-type:inline-size; container-name:lo. Establishes the WIDE/NARROW tier breakpoint.

`.lo-panel` (each trinity panel) and `.lo-row` (each narrow-tier compact program row): their own nested container-type:inline-size, so each hero numeral's cqi resolves against ITS OWN column/row width, not the whole window.
typeRamp: --lo-fs-hero (trinity hero numeral, WIDE): clamp(64px, 34cqi, 116px) of .lo-panel's own width
--lo-fs-hero-narrow (trinity numeral, NARROW compact row): clamp(32px, 9cqi, 48px) of .lo-row's own width
--lo-fs-slab (masthead one-word verdict): clamp(28px, 5cqi, 44px) of .lo-eva
--lo-fs-strain (neural strain hero number, subordinate to trinity): clamp(26px, 4.5cqi, 38px)
--lo-fs-body (all VT323 descriptions/sentence lines): clamp(19px, 1cqi + 17px, 21px), pinned so it NEVER breaches the system's stated 19-21px VT323 floor even though it is still nominally fluid
--lo-fs-label (Silkscreen annotation labels/eyebrows): clamp(9px, 0.6cqi + 8px, 11px)
--lo-fs-pill (bay pill / mode chip text): clamp(9px, 0.5cqi + 8.5px, 10.5px)
--lo-fs-tick (gutter operator tick label / value): label clamp(8px, 0.4cqi + 7.5px, 9px), value clamp(12px, 0.8cqi + 10px, 14px)
fluid.columns: CSS Grid with fr units, not fixed pixel columns. WIDE tier: `.lo-eva { grid-template-columns: 132px 1fr; grid-template-areas: 'mast mast' 'gutter trinity' 'support support' 'foot foot'; }`; the trinity row internally `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)`. NARROW tier: single column, `grid-template-areas: 'mast' 'tabs' 'page' 'foot'`.
fluid.breakpoint: One binary container-query breakpoint on `.lo-eva`: `@container lo (min-width: 800px)` applies the WIDE-tier rules (gutter sidebar + 3-col monumental trinity + 3-across support band, everything visible at once, no tabs); below 800px content inline-size is the NARROW tier (gutter collapses to a horizontal strip, trinity becomes the compact-list `.lo-row` arrangement, support band stacks, and a 2-tab strip - PROGRAMS / RIG & STATUS - pages between the trinity and the gutter+support content, with the masthead persistent above both tabs). 800px is chosen so the four VIEWPORT token widths split 2/2: 480px and 760px content land NARROW, 860px and 940px land WIDE.

reflowOrder.4:3 (window width 480px, --kp-win-w-narr: masthead (verdict+chips wrap to 2 rows) -> PROGRAMS/RIG&STATUS tab strip -> active tab page (compact-list trinity, or gutter-strip+bays+pouch+strain stacked) -> footline
reflowOrder.16:9 (window width 860px, --kp-win-w-wid: masthead single row -> hazard divider -> gutter column (left, 132px) beside trinity 3-column row (right) -> hazard divider -> support band, bays|pouch|strain 3 across -> footline
reflowOrder.21:9 (window width 940px, --kp-win-w-her: identical order to 16:9, with more breathing room (wider trinity columns, descriptions wrap to fewer lines)
reflowOrder.1280x800 laptop (window width 760px, --k: identical order to 4:3 - this is the historically-critical case (the brief's original footprint complaint), so it deliberately degrades to the same proven-safe compact pattern rather than a bespoke third arrangement
reflowOrder.narrow <=760px (general case, reachable: identical to the laptop case; the 760px threshold used for the laptop token IS the brief's literal narrow cutoff, so that scenario doubles as the narrow-reflow proof

fluid.note: the underlying rules are continuous (any container width works via cqi+container-query), not four fixed layouts; the four VIEWPORT buttons are convenient, meaningful checkpoints for review (each pinned to an existing --kp-win-w-* token), not an exhaustive enumeration. Height budget is a design target, not a literal CSS max-height clip: WIDE tier's tallest realistic content (DAY 4 run state) is estimated at roughly 700-720px; NARROW tier's tallest single tab page is estimated at roughly 580-620px; both comfortably clear the brief's 820px ceiling with margin. If the live build runs over, the named cuts/paging above are the fallback, not a scrollbar.

viewportRig.mechanism: Exactly one `.lo-stage` bezel is visible at a time; clicking a VIEWPORT rig button swaps which stage is shown (matching the existing rig convention of one active state per group). Each `.lo-stage` is an illustrative aspect-ratio frame at a REAL representative resolution (not artificially compressed to fit the demo page), containing the `.term` window at a fixed width pinned to an existing --kp-win-w-* token, plus a thin 44px `.lo-stage-bar` bottom strip (matching .kp-taskbar's height) for visual grounding only, not a pixel-exact fit proof. Selecting 21:9 legitimately widens the outer page, requiring the reviewer to scroll horizontally, which is an accepted, narrow extension of the same outer-page-scroll allowance every study already uses for vertical scroll under a short viewport.

crt.onConstruction: A new `.lo-crt` overlay, `position:absolute;inset:0;pointer-events:none;` scoped to `.lo-stage` (which is `position:relative`), not `position:fixed` over the whole page like the base `.kp-crt` - the CRT glass belongs to the simulated monitor, not the review chrome around it. Five stacked layers, bottom to top: (1) SCANLINES: repeating-linear-gradient 0deg, black 0/1px transparent 1px/2px (2px pitch, tighter than the floor .kp-crt's 3px pitch), opacity 0.26, mix-blend-mode:multiply. (2) SHADOW MASK: repeating-linear-gradient 90deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.08) 0/1px transparent 1px/3px (kept MONOCHROME, not RGB-fringed, specifically to hold the single-ink-accent law even in the CRT glass layer). (3) BLOOM (new, not in the floor version): radial-gradient(140% 100% at 50% 40%, var(--px-glow) 0%, transparent 60%), opacity ~0.12, mix-blend-mode:screen - uses the SAME ink token as everything else, so it still passes the single-ink law and recolors correctly under every hue including amber. (4) ROLL (new): a ~120px-tall soft horizontal band, `background:linear-gradient(180deg,transparent,var(--px-glow),transparent)` at opacity ~0.06, mix-blend-mode:screen, animated via a new keyframe `lo-crt-roll` (translateY from -20% to 120% of the stage height), `animation: lo-crt-roll 16s steps(32) infinite` (stepped, not eased, per house law); disabled/hidden under prefers-reduced-motion. (5) VIGNETTE (heavier than the floor): radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 45%, transparent 45%, rgba(0,0,0,0.72) 100%), normal blend, topmost so corners always read darkest regardless of bloom/roll passing beneath.
crt.offConstruction: CRT OFF removes all 5 `.lo-crt` layers entirely (not just opacity to 0); nothing else on the page changes. This works because none of the page's own richness lives inside the CRT layer: text glow (text-shadow on .lo-num/.lo-slab/.kp-hero), the dither/checker background texture (.term-body::before), hazard stripes, and corner brackets are all authored directly on content elements, independent of CRT presence. OFF is therefore a clean flat-ink print by construction, not by extra effort.
crt.blendModeSummary: multiply (scanlines, mask, both darkening) -> screen (bloom, roll, both brightening) -> normal (vignette, final darken pass on top)

amber.reasoning: Follows the existing lavender block's own documented discipline ('compensated for CRT darkening'): --ch is chosen bright/saturated (#ffab3d) rather than a muted 'true' amber, specifically so it survives this study's heavier 5-layer CRT stack (multiply scanlines+mask, screen bloom+roll, a final normal vignette) without sinking toward brown/grey, the way a duller orange would. --px-void (#100a04) is a warm dark brown-black, matching the pattern of the other three hue blocks each tinting their void toward their own hue family (lavender blue-violet, magenta red-violet, phosphor green). --ch2 (#c2431a) is a deeper, more saturated rust, hue-shifted away from --ch the same way magenta's ch2 shifts toward violet away from its pink ch. --ch-hot (#fff2d9) is a warm ivory-white highlight, matching the other three blocks' 'pushed to near-white' hot tone.

items.spec:
Builds `ui-demos/solder-v3/index.html`, replacing `ui-demos/solder/` as the SOLDER.BAY study. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, matching every other ui-demos study; links `../_shared/kp.css` + `../_shared/system.css` + the Silkscreen/VT323/IBM-Plex-Mono Google Fonts stack. Reuses the loadout-eva reference build verbatim: the true-resolution-then-transform-scale viewport rig (`.lo-fit`/`.lo-stage`/`.lo-warp`, loadout-eva/index.html lines 157-238, `fit()`/`measure()` lines 1783-1814), the six-layer CRT glass (`g-scan`/`g-mask`/`g-bloom`/`g-spec`/`g-vig`/`g-bezel`, CSS lines 264-329, markup lines 1139-1146, rescoped to this study's own stage), the `:root[data-scheme="nerv"]`/`"tokyo"` role-token blocks and the `:root` collapse defaults (lines 44-141), and the `countUp`/`typeIn`/`radioRow` demo-rig helpers (lines 1329-1362, 1706-1718). New class prefix `sv-` (SOLDER V3), paralleling loadout's `lo-` prefix. Root frame keeps the shared `.term`/`.term-bar`/`.term-body` standalone-study naming (not `.kp-fw*`, reserved for the desktop iframe embed), 3px solid `var(--r-hazard)` border (matching loadout's window-edge role choice, not the round-1 study's plain `var(--ch)` border), the shared 9px/26px drop-shadow filter, solid-ink title bar reading SOLDER.BAY with the standard 3-glyph decorative cluster.

THE CENTRAL MOVE. The round-1 bench has no focal element because it puts a MID-weight schematic, a MID-weight rack, and a HERO-weight floating `.kp-hero-slot` (`Hero text="JOIN"`, solder.tsx:401, present in only 1 of 4 interaction states) on one plane: three things compete for the eye, and one of them only exists sometimes. This item deletes the floating JOIN hero-slot entirely (see cuts) and promotes the shipped minor boxed WORKPIECE datarow (solder.tsx:387-390) into the surface's one focal element at extreme scale. This directly answers the brief's first hard decision: the hero is a READOUT (what the surface is telling you), not the interactive surface itself. The rack (where the hands actually go) stays mid-weight and is the SECOND most important zone, not the first, because a tap target sized for extreme scale would waste the surface's limited width on one slot at the cost of the other four; extreme-scaling a control, not a reading, would also violate law 2's own 'one focal element' rule the instant a second slot tried to compete for the same treatment. This mirrors LOADOUT.CFG's own resolution (hero numerals = readout = focal; mode-chip buttons = the actual controls = mid-weight) applied to a tool window instead of a status window.

FOCAL ELEMENT ACROSS ALL FOUR INTERACTION STATES (full state table in `focalElement` below): the hero glyph is always answering the SAME question, 'what shape is the reading in front of you', which is what keeps it legibly focal instead of merely big. It renders `pouch[held]`'s own shape noun and arm count while holding-without-candidate, or the legal UNION's shape noun and arm count the instant a candidate locks (tap-pair or drag-hover-legal), reusing the EXISTING `schem`/`candidate`/`held` values solder.tsx already computes every render (the `schem` useMemo, lines 367-377) verbatim: zero new state fields, zero reducer changes, a pure presentational promotion. A small state-driven eyebrow label above the glyph (`// WORKPIECE _` while holding-only, flipping to `// JOIN RESULT _` the instant a legal candidate locks; `JOIN RESULT` is a bare 2-word label coined here, not sentence-shaped, no copy order needed per the loadout `OPERATOR RIG`/`PLACE COST` precedent) keeps the word JOIN alive as a naming label without a second hero-weight element carrying it. At true idle the glyph shows a large dashed placeholder AT THE HERO GLYPH'S OWN FOOTPRINT, never a shrunk idle treatment, satisfying law 4's equal-footprint rule at the hero itself, not just the rack.

THE SCHEMATIC (round-1's own ruling preserved verbatim: a diegetic diagram, not decorative art, so law 8 rule 1 never applies to it) becomes a small satellite plate beside/above the hero glyph inside the SAME zone, fixed at 168x126px (exactly the 304:228 native viewBox ratio, so nothing distorts), reusing the `Schematic` component's SVG structure (solder.tsx lines 81-118) verbatim. Because it is live SVG vector art, not a 1-bit dither raster, law 5's crop-not-scale rule (which governs raster dither assets specifically) does not constrain its size at all; it resizes in the viewBox's own coordinate space exactly the way the patch glyphs already do at multiple sizes elsewhere on this same surface (GLYPH=44 in the rack, 16/20 in the join preview, 34 in the LAST WELD chip). Colour AND size keep it from competing with the hero glyph beside it: it renders in `--r-aux` (see roleTokens.aux) at a fixed modest size, while the hero glyph is `--r-data` at extreme, viewport-responsive scale, so the eye lands on the glyph first every time.

COMPOSITOR-SAFE MOTION CONVERSIONS (full inventory with property/timing/trigger in `motion` below, plus a frame-timing acceptance target). The round-1 study's ghost-chip follow (`transition: left 40ms steps(2), top 40ms steps(2)`, ui-demos/solder/index.html:197) and the fuse timeline's two-waypoint chip travel (raw JS `style.left`/`style.top` assignments at t=40/80ms, index.html:868-875) both animate LAYOUT properties. v3 repositions both via `transform:translate(x,y)` on a `position:fixed;left:0;top:0` base instead, keeping the identical 40ms steps(2) cadence and the identical t=40/80ms waypoint timing, and unifying what were two different techniques into one. The legal-hover pulse (`slot-legal-pulse`, index.html:200-201) and the deny flash (`slot-deny-flash`, index.html:203-207) both animate a PAINT property (`background`). v3 rebuilds both as a promoted `::after` overlay animating `opacity` on a fixed `--r-ok`/`--r-warn` tinted plate, reusing loadout-eva's own `.lo-riskflash` pattern verbatim (index.html:863-873, a `mix-blend-mode:difference` plate, measured 9.3ms p95 against a 9.0ms do-nothing baseline versus 50ms p95 for the paint-property equivalent under the CRT glass). Every other moving thing on the surface (spark burst, weld-dot fade-in, rack slot reveal, deck shake, the schematic's gain-arm blink, the status box caret) is ALREADY built on `opacity`/`transform` in kp.css/system.css/solder.tsx and is reused verbatim with no property change.

items.focalElement: The hero glyph (Z1) is the surface's one focal element at extreme scale, and it answers the SAME question in all 4 interaction states rather than switching roles, which is what keeps it legibly focal instead of merely big: 'what shape is the reading in front of you'. IDLE (nothing held): a large dashed placeholder glyph at the hero glyph's own footprint (never a smaller idle treatment), eyebrow '// WORKPIECE _', no arm-count caption; Z2 reads LINE_IDLE ('PICK A PIECE.'). roleTokens.data: Hot values, the biggest glyphs on the surface: the Z1 hero glyph itself (the single focal element), the schematic's GAIN arms (the partner-contributed arms, still blinking on the shipped `kp-cursor-blink` 0.9s steps(2) cadence, solder.tsx's `.arm-gain`, reused verbatim) and the hub, both chip VALUES in Z4 (POUCH n/5, and the LAST WELD glyph fill, matching loadout's own chip-value convention), and the spark burst plus weld-dot afterglow (the commit-moment motion; a forge-hot instant, not a risk instant, see motion for why this is not r-warn or r-hazard).

roleTokens.warn: RISK, ruled explicitly per the brief's demand. This surface has no strain meter, so r-warn is reserved for the one genuinely alarm-shaped moment: an ACTIVE REJECTION EVENT, meaning the instant the player actually attempts an illegal action (a live, pointer-tracked drag-hover over an illegal target, inherently transient since it vanishes the moment the pointer moves off it, or a completed illegal drop/tap, the one-shot deny flash). It does NOT extend to the passive DEAD/disabled resting state (a piece with no legal partner sitting dimmed with its diagonal slash, potentially on up to 4 of the 5 slots at once for the whole duration a piece is held): colouring that state r-warn would put multiple red shapes on screen simultaneously every single time a piece is picked up, which is exactly the habituation failure loadout-eva's own round-3 gate found and had to fix the other direction ('a page with five red-family shapes on every healthy visit trains the eye to stop sampling hue and fill for the one time it matters', loadout-eva/NOTES.md). DEAD stays a neutral, colour-absent r-struct-derived tone (see struct above); r-warn only ever appears as (a) the live hover-illegal border, present only while a pointer is actually over that specific slot mid-drag, (b) the one-shot deny-flash overlay, which also moves (see motion), satisfying law 1's 'colour never carries risk alone' requirement at the one moment risk is real, and (c) Z2's status line ink specifically when NO_JOIN_LINE is showing because of an active rejection, never the passive zero-partners case, which stays r-line.
roleTokens.aux: A different signal class, ruled per the brief's invitation: the SCHEMATIC plate claims it, specifically its grid backdrop, the hole marker at true idle, and the BASE arms (the piece's own already-committed geometry). This is a genuine second signal class from the rack's interactive-state colours and from the hero glyph's hot data colour, the same 'a different signal class' distinction loadout-eva draws for its camera feed. The schematic's GAIN arms are deliberately carved OUT of r-aux and into r-data instead (see data above), because they represent the thing about to change, which is r-data's job everywhere else on the surface; this keeps r-aux meaning 'the steady read' and r-data meaning 'what's hot or changing' consistently across both the schematic and the hero glyph.
roleTokens.hazard: Structural red: the window frame border (matching loadout's `.term{border:3px solid var(--r-hazard)}` exactly), the Z1 heavy corner brackets (the ONLY corner brackets on the surface, scoped per law 4), and the '// PLACEMENT' hazard-stripe divider. HEADLINE DECISION (law 2, the hard problem this window poses: a CLI is a flat text stream with no natural focal element, and the shipped study puts 973 lines of output at one weight in one 20px stream). The focal element is ONE FOCAL CELL, top-left of the window, whose CONTENT moves through four states rather than staying fixed, exactly the brief's own suggested answer to a surface whose focus genuinely moves: PENDING (a blinking placeholder, ambient, during the three-hop dial, eyebrow ROUTE), OFFER (tonight's price as a giant numeral, `--r-data`, eyebrow RATE, the default resting state whenever the market is open and nothing has landed yet this connection), REVEAL (the just-landed patch glyph at hero scale plus its SHAPE/ARMS/GUARANTEE rows, `--r-aux`, eyebrow SIGNAL DROP, persists as 'the last drop' until a further BUY replaces it or the channel drops), and DEAD (MARKET OFFLINE or NO CARRIER at alarm scale, `--r-warn`, eyebrow ROUTE, whenever the channel is not live). All four states share ONE FIXED footprint, `.dn-focal{min-height:216px}` including its 1px hairline border, sized to the REVEAL state's tallest real content (eyebrow + hero + a 3-row block), so switching states never reflows the window: RULINGS law 4's equal-footprint rule for empty/filled SLOTS, generalized here to empty/filled STATES of the one focal panel. OFFER's 3-row block reuses the shipped LIST card's own three rows verbatim (ITEM 'PATCH PIECE', SHAPE 'UNSORTED', STOCK 'A CRATE FULL', darknet.tsx:315-318) as a preview of what a drop will show, so REVEAL's SHAPE/ARMS/GUARANTEE rows land in the identical row-block height with zero accepted dead space. DEAD's row-block reuses the shipped follow-up line verbatim ('Signal only holds after the shop shuts. Trades resume at day close.', darknet.tsx:509,550) wrapped small under the hero text, filling the same space usefully; NO CARRIER's row-block is the one accepted exception (left blank, matching loadout-eva's own accepted-dead-space precedent for its SCAN/DEFEND panels), since the window closes 900ms after entering it and has nothing further to say. This one move demotes the shipped 5-chip status strip's RATE chip entirely (its number now lives ONLY in the focal cell, never duplicated at two scales and positions) and pulls the SIGNAL DROP reveal card and its 108px glyph cell out of the log entirely, which is this redesign's single biggest structural move and its single biggest height saving. IDENTITY, LAW 1's standing note. The stepped-notch title bar (`.kp-frame-notched-bar`, system.css:118-121, clip-path unchanged), the double-chevron mark (`chevMark()`, darknet.tsx:98-118, DOM-ported verbatim, second stroke hot), the 3-bar weak-signal meter with its tall bar cutting out (unchanged shipped CSS, kept on base `--ch`/`--px-void`, not remapped to a role, since it is pure identity flavor unconnected to any real state), and the log's heavier dither (8px `--ch2` checker OVER the 4px `--ch` grain, ui-demos/darknet/index.html:96-99, reused verbatim) are the ONLY things carrying this window's otherness, and they get no softer under v3: same clip-path, same bitmap, same two-layer dither density. `--ch2` (the v2 support tone, still defined per scheme block) stays reserved for this identity texture and for the vendor-adjacent dither only, never repurposed as a ninth role. GLANCE ORDER (see glanceOrderSummary/zones/fluid for the enforcing numbers). 1st the focal cell (extreme scale, the only decision this window asks for). 2nd the status strip (ROUTE/PEER/BAL/POUCH, four small chips, demoted from five once RATE folds into the focal cell). 3rd the log (dense reading, not the first hit but the bulk of the surface's content). Deliberately ambient, never competing: the title bar's identity chrome, the prompt, the trade-chip row, the footline. Law 8's structural lesson is spent here exactly as loadout-eva spent it: the focal cell and the status strip SHARE one row (`grid-template-areas:"focal status"`), so the four short status chips cost nothing extra, where isolating them onto their own row would have cost roughly 60-70px. DENY VS ALARM, LAW 5's explicit ask ('assign SHORT and POUCH FULL a different role explicitly so nobody reaches for red twice'). `--r-warn` has exactly one owner on this surface, the dead-channel alarm, covering MARKET OFFLINE, the dead-relay hop's 'dead air' verdict word, 'carrier lost.', and the NO CARRIER teardown (all four named in the brief). SHORT ('// SHORT _ NEED {cost} CR. YOU HOLD {credits} CR.', darknet.tsx:353) takes `--r-hazard` instead, a static (never-animating) inverse-video flood, the SAME structural red already ambient elsewhere on this surface (the window border, the stripes, the UNREGISTERED CHANNEL line, the focal brackets) but never the alarm's hotter, purer, moving red. This mirrors loadout-eva's own hazard/warn split exactly (hazard = ambient structural red that never moves, warn = the one thing that does) and gives SHORT a look that is clearly 'red, this failed' without ever being mistaken for 'the channel is dying'. POUCH FULL stays exactly as shipped, a vendor-voiced deny line only ('Dealer is not a storage locker...', darknet.tsx:348) with no boxed marker at all, matching the existing asymmetry between the two denies rather than inventing one. WHY ONLY THE FOCAL CELL CARRIES THE ALARM'S MOTION. The alarm's colour and inverse-video channels appear on THREE elements at once when the channel dies (the focal cell, the ROUTE chip, and the log's own hero line, all sharing the SAME dead-channel state), but only the FOCAL CELL carries the composited difference-blend PULSE (`.dn-alarm-flash`, `mix-blend-mode:difference`, `opacity` on a promoted layer, `will-change:opacity`, `1.2s steps(2)` infinite, redeclared locally from the exact technique at loadout-eva/index.html:851-873, `.lo-riskflash`/`lo-risk-blink`). This mirrors loadout-eva's OWN internal precedent exactly: even within its one risk moment, only the strain NUMBER carries the difference-blend pulse while the strain BAR's segments take colour+inverse only, no independent animation. Three simultaneously-pulsing red elements would read as noisy rather than legible, and RULINGS' performance law prefers fewer promoted, animating layers over more; the ROUTE chip and the log's hero line get the static flood (2 of 3 channels) and never animate on their own. `.dn-hero` (the log's alarm-owned hero-line class) therefore HAS no non-alarm use on this surface, since darknet.tsx's only two `kp-dnet-hero` usages (MARKET OFFLINE, NO CARRIER, darknet.tsx:462,506,547) are both now alarm-owned; it is demoted from the shipped 40px clamp to `--dn-fs-loghero: clamp(20px, calc(4cqi + 12px), 28px)` now that the focal cell carries the surface's primary alarm-scale statement. THE TELEGRAPH-COLOUR DISTINCTION (a deliberate stylistic echo of the duel's own two-beat aim-then-strike law, not a claim that this IS the duel mechanic). The dotsLine beats are restructured from ONE text node (the shipped `label + dots + verdict` concatenation, darknet.tsx:208-228) into TWO inline spans so the verdict word can carry its own colour independent of the label: `{label} {dots}LINKED` or `dead air`, the verdict span appended only on the final tick once the outcome is known. 'dead air' (the aim/telegraph beat for the alarm that is about to land) gets ONLY the `--r-warn` colour, no inverse video, no motion; the alarm's full three-channel strike lands one beat later when MARKET OFFLINE actually pushes. 'LINKED' and the escrow handoff's 'DONE' verdict take `--r-ok`. ROLE ASSIGNMENTS. All eight are listed exhaustively in the `roles` field below, cross-referenced from the brief's own partial list (struct/note/line/data/ok/hazard) plus this item's own reasoning for warn (above) and aux. One departure from loadout-eva's literal practice, stated explicitly per the house style: loadout-eva mostly left plain chrome borders on `--ch-dim`/`--ch-faint` and reserved `--r-struct` for a single bezel; this surface applies `--r-struct` broadly and literally to every plain chrome border (the brief specifically calls struct out as one of the 'boring' roles needing explicit, visible ownership, and RULINGS' own table defines it as 'panel frames, dividers, disabled outlines', which is exactly this usage). AWAY FROM ANY GATE. Per RULINGS 'Process' and the brief, this is a pure-UI redesign of an existing window: no loremaster, no tutorial gate. One gate-shaped observation is flagged here rather than assumed away: folding RATE into the focal cell removes the standalone chip the shipped integration's own tutorial gate added (darknet-cli-rate-chip, ux-2026-07-29-darknet-cli's addendum, 'tonight's price stays readable at a glance, no command required'). The focal cell's OFFER state satisfies that same fact even more directly (a hero numeral beats a 13px chip for 'readable at a glance'), so this is read as strengthening the fix, not undoing it, but it is named here so the Tutorial Agent can confirm at gate time rather than have the change arrive unannounced.

items.spec:
Builds `ui-demos/kpos-desktop-v3/index.html`, a standalone redesign of the whole KP/OS desktop shell (boot, login, wallpaper furniture, icon grid, ticker, taskbar, start menu, window chrome) to the v3 instrument-panel system, replacing `ui-demos/kpos-desktop/` as the study under review. `kernel-panic-site/app/src/components/os/{shop-os,boot,login,desk,wm,icons,kp-ui}.tsx` and `wm.css` are read for STRUCTURE/state-flow/exact copy only; nothing in kernel-panic-site/ is touched. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, following the loadout-eva build recipe (RULINGS.md section 9) verbatim: `<link>` `../_shared/kp.css` + `../_shared/system.css` + the Silkscreen/VT323/IBM-Plex-Mono Google Fonts stack, `body{overflow:auto;display:block;height:auto;min-height:100%;padding:26px 16px 40px;}`, the real-resolution viewport rig transform-scaled to fit (`.lo-fit`/`.lo-fitwrap`/`.lo-stage`/`.lo-warp`/`.lo-overscan`/`.lo-desk`/`.lo-deskwrap`/`.lo-free`/`.lo-stage-bar`, copied verbatim renamed `ds-`), the six-layer FLAT/OFF CRT glass (copied verbatim, NO CURVED per RULINGS law 6, ONE tube over the whole desk not per-window, replacing the shipped `.kp-crt` fixed overlay entirely), and the role-token block (`:root`, `:root[data-scheme="nerv"]`, `:root[data-scheme="tokyo"]`, hexes never retyped).

HEADLINE DECISION (ruling 14's scope, answered here per the brief). The shell itself now carries `data-scheme` the same way `data-hue` does today: the start menu's HUE cycle becomes a SCHEME cycle (NERV / TOKYO NIGHT), writing `document.documentElement.dataset.scheme`. With no scheme set, `:root`'s own defaults collapse every `--r-*` role onto the single `--ch`/`--ch2`/`--ch-hot` accent, so the shell renders bit-identical to the shipped v2 desktop; this reversibility is demonstrated directly by adding a third SCHEME option, DEFAULT (the `data-scheme`-unset collapse), to the switch alongside the two named schemes, because the brief's own stated purpose for this cycle ('the demo exists so the user can see that decision before anyone integrates it') cannot be shown with only two options on the row. The page still LOADS on NERV per the brief's literal instruction; DEFAULT is one click away on the same switch, not buried in CSS.

STRUCTURE, UNCHANGED. Every piece of current anatomy the brief lists survives: the 1700ms six-line BIOS boot card, the 3-slot login with typed access and TEST SOUND, the wallpaper's dither field, 4 registration crosses, WallPoster and WallScope, the 8-icon grid with INBOX's badge and slot-in stagger, the ticker at `steps(140)`, the 44px taskbar with its chip cluster and ABANDON modal, the 5-item start menu, and window chrome's 3px border / solid-ink bar / pixel-X / drag-clamp / focus-pulse / DARKNET stepped-notch / overflow-visible no-scrollbar body. Nothing here is a new window or a new mechanic; this is recolouring (roles) and refluiding (cqi), not reinvention.

THE DESK IS A CONTAINER TOO. Shell furniture (taskbar, ticker, icons, wallpaper, boot, login) sizes 'against the viewport' per the brief, but RULINGS law 3 bans `vw` absolutely. Reconciled by wrapping the whole stage in ONE container: `.ds-stage{container-type:inline-size;container-name:desk}` (the same element the CRT glass and the viewport rig already scale as a unit). Every shell clamp() resolves against `desk`, which in practice equals the viewport width, so 'sizes against the viewport' and 'never vw' are simultaneously true. Per-window chrome (title bar text, close glyph, taskbar-independent) keeps its OWN nested container on each `.kp-fw` frame, matching every other v3 panel, so a window's chrome scales to ITS tile once that window's own content is redesigned in a future cycle; this cycle only needs the chrome ramp to exist and be non-`vw`, since window BODIES stay out of scope.

THE IDLE DESK GETS A REAL FOCAL ELEMENT. The brief states the desktop's focal element is the focused window, but names a second case to resolve: the idle desk, reachable by logging into a slot with no active run and manually closing SHOPFRONT.EXE (the flow window only auto-reopens on a `screen` transition, so a deliberately-closed idle desk is a real, reachable state, not a hypothetical). An idle desk with no window open has nothing to focus by the existing law, so this spec promotes the WallPoster's ATTEMPT/DAY pair into a genuine hero readout at extreme scale (matching law 2's own contrast device rather than inventing new furniture): the two numerals print far larger than anything else on the empty desk, `--r-data` (they are exactly the 'day/credits values' the brief already assigns that role), with the door-state line and wordmark demoted beneath as identity dressing. This reads as a diagnostic bench proudly displaying its own status even before the operator touches anything, and gives the promised law-2 statement ('one focal element, at extreme scale') an honest owner instead of leaving the idle desk hierarchy-less.

STRAIN THRESHOLD CORRECTION (flagged in `notes`). run-reducer.ts's strain is a depleting resource (START_STRAIN 100, `Math.max(0, run.strain - chip)`, the run ends at 0), matching every other strain readout in the game including loadout-eva's own 'risk at or below 35' framing. The shipped taskbar chip's `run.strain > 70` danger class is therefore backwards from the fiction: it would light the alarm at FULL health and stay unlit while the run is dying. This spec wires the v3 alarm to the correct low band (`<= 35`, matching loadout-eva's own number for cross-window consistency) rather than propagating what reads as a display bug into the surface whose entire job this cycle is to make risk legible.

items.spec: Builds `ui-demos/dive-v3/index.html`, a standalone redesign of DIVE.EXE to the v3 instrument-panel system, replacing `ui-demos/dive/` as the study under review. The whole flood-claim duel (board generation, reducer, opponent AI, legality, traps, par, patch pieces, end conditions) imports verbatim from `kernel-panic-site/app/src/game/` via a `dive.ts` bundle exactly like the old study, so behaviour and numbers cannot drift; `components/game/{duel,duel-board}.tsx` and the `.dv-*` block in `styles.css` are read for STRUCTURE/state-flow/exact-copy only, nothing in kernel-panic-site/ is touched. Playable end to end. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, following the loadout-eva build recipe: the Google Fonts stack, the real-resolution viewport rig transform-scaled to fit (renamed `dv-`), the six-layer FLAT/OFF CRT glass copied verbatim (NO CURVED), and the role-token block copied verbatim. UNLIKE every windowed panel, DIVE.EXE is full-screen and real-time per the brief's SEQUENCING NOTE: no `.term`/`.kp-fw` chrome, no 700px window-tiling height ceiling, `.dv-stage{container-type:inline-size}` fills the whole viewport instead of a window tile. Every other law applies in full, including the hard 'no internal scrollbars, ever' rule, which DIVE.EXE must satisfy without the escape hatch a height ceiling gives a window (see BUS.LOG below). GLANCE ORDER (law 2, answered explicitly per the brief's either/or). The BOARD is the ambient focal element: the single largest object on the stage by area (target ~60-64% of stage width at the wide end), always the biggest thing on screen, satisfying law 2's 'extreme scale' the way a full-bleed game board naturally does rather than via a numeral. Within it, THE TELEGRAPH (dashed aim brackets + INTENT line + virus card) is the ONE thing permitted to INTERRUPT the board's own stillness: the instant `state.oppTurn.aim` is set, the telegraph claims the eye via colour + its own dedicated blink, exactly the 'motion is what motion is for' carve-out law 7 names for it. RAM/ROUND/STRAIN, tied for co-equal weight today, are explicitly demoted: none of the three rail numerals is allowed to read as a page headline; they sit in the SAME type class as the rail's other mono values, sized for legibility, not for competing with the board. Full order: 1st BOARD (ambient) with TELEGRAPH as its interrupt-focal layer; 2nd LEFT RAIL program keys (the verbs, always live, RAM box included); 3rd RIGHT RAIL turn pair + route-threat rows (see r-warn below); 4th the rail's demoted numerals (RAM/ROUND/PAR/STRAIN, same weight class as rail body text, clearly smaller than the key labels); ambient/lowest: BUS.LOG, the device photo, hex-corner/ruler board dressing, the watermark. RISK OWNER (law 1, the brief's named two-candidate choice). `--r-warn` is the ROUTE-THREAT system: the qualitative YOUR ROUTE / ITS ROUTE datarows and the two centre-board threat banners, whichever direction fires (YOUR ROUTE = SEVERED, ITS ROUTE = CLOSING or AT THE CORE, AT THE CORE running a faster pulse cadence as the same alarm's hottest tier, not a second alarm). This beats the strain candidate because strain (`props.strain`) is a pre-dive snapshot passed in from the run layer, static for the whole dive rather than something the player reacts to turn by turn, while route-threat is the live, moment-to-moment fact the two-program toolkit exists to answer ('rotate here, block there, right now'). Everything else that shares the shipped `kp-datarow-warn` treatment TODAY (STRAIN in its low band, ARMED NODES hidden-trap mismatch, BANKED RAM, PAR over-budget) is explicitly DEMOTED to `--r-hazard`: same static colour+inverse flood, never the alarm's motion, so nobody reaches for warn twice. The INTRUSION side (its territory fill, its port, its turn-cell, its aim brackets and virus card) is `--r-hazard` as its permanent structural identity, per the brief's own steer; the aim brackets keep their OWN event-tied blink (per-opponent-turn, not idle ambience) as a SEPARATE motion channel from the warn alarm's, matching law 5's point that this surface is allowed to be the most animated in the game as long as each motion means something. FLUID RAILS (law 4). Both fixed rails (236px left, 264px right) become clamp() on cqi against `.dv-stage`'s own container, exactly as fluid as a windowed panel's rails, just resolving against the fullscreen stage instead of a tile. One binary 700px breakpoint is declared for law compliance; it never fires on any supported viewport (the 1280px laptop floor clears it by 580px), so all three render the identical three-column arrangement, board scaling in the centre. NO SCROLLBARS holds absolutely including BUS.LOG: the log keeps its full 40-line ring buffer in state, but the VISIBLE region is a fixed-height, `overflow:hidden` clip sized to whatever the rail's available height allows (roughly 10-16 lines depending on viewport); new lines append at the bottom and old lines fall off the clipped top, exactly the mechanism the old study already used, never a scroll thumb. DEVICE PHOTO (law 5). KEPT, not cut: the shipped art (`roster-art.ts`'s device macros, native ~880x880) is a single coherent close-up subject, not a busy multi-panel schematic, so it should read fine at a small crop the way a busy schematic would not. It is served today at `width={880} height={880}` inside a narrow rail cell, which is almost certainly browser-downscaled today, a direct law-5 violation under v3. This spec converts it to a 1:1 CROP inside a small fixed-pixel viewport (matching loadout-eva's LIVE MONITOR bezel mechanism exactly: `overflow:hidden`, the `` at its native intrinsic size, positioned via negative top/left offsets, zero resampling), `--r-aux`, with the three FEED treatments (INK TINT default / TRUE 1-BIT / FULL COLOUR) per law 5, reusing loadout-eva's colourisation generator verbatim if FULL COLOUR is exercised. NO COUNTDOWN NUMBERS survives unchanged from the old study's own ruling: route rows stay qualitative (OPEN/SEVERED/CLOSING/CUT/AT THE CORE), no surface ever prints a rotation distance.

## What this replaces and what stays

Rebuilds StoryScene (kernel-panic-site/app/src/components/game/screens.tsx), the story-beat player shared by six callers: dayOpenScene (fronts as window title MORNING.LOG), runOpenerScene, runEndScene, finaleWinScene, tutorialIntroScene, tutorialOutroScene (the last five front as SHOPFRONT.EXE per shop-os.tsx's title switch). Design target is the dayOpenScene case; the other five are addressed under 'How the other callers land' below. Everything from the shipped surface survives in some form: the persistent corner day tag (generalized into the focal numeral), the optional still/portrait per beat (generalized into one fixed image-stage cell), speaker name + lines, the pulsing next-glyph (folded into the NEXT/CONTINUE control), and sfx('story') firing on advance (kept, unchanged). Nothing is dropped outright; see 'Cuts' for the one real footprint cost.

## Glance order and the focal decision

1st (focal, extreme scale): the DAY/RUN numeral in the masthead. 2nd: the current beat's spoken/system text in the text panel (where the player actually reads). 3rd: the image-stage cell (Rhea's counter camera or the back room camera), supporting and diegetic, not competing on scale. Ambient (never competes; unboxed, --r-note or --r-struct, smallest sizes on the surface): the eyebrow line, the register/back-room status chip, the beat-progress dots, the speaker name chip.

Defends the numeral over the spoken line, per the brief's fork: a dialogue box is a field of even body type by nature (law 2's stated trap), so the ONE thing that can carry extreme scale without breaking the VT323 19-21px body floor is the thing that is not prose, the day/run index. The body copy stays fixed at --ml-fs-body: clamp(19px, calc(1cqi + 17px), 21px) (copied verbatim from loadout-eva's --lo-fs-body formula) at every one of the three supported viewports; it never grows to compete and is never asked to. The numeral is --ml-fs-num: clamp(76px, 10cqi, 128px), resolving against the outer .ml-eva container (no nested per-column container, unlike loadout's trinity, since this surface has no repeated sub-panel needing independent scaling). Measured against that container at each supported window width: 860px window (content 832px, cqi=8.32) -> numeral 83px vs body 21px = 3.95x; 940px window (content 912px, cqi=9.12) -> 91px vs 21px = 4.33x; 760px laptop window (content 732px, cqi=7.32, clamps to the 76px floor) -> 76px vs 21px = 3.62x. All three clear the 2x law-2 minimum by a wide margin, and none of them is close to the floor case (a surface whose largest element is 1.3x the second largest has no hierarchy; this one never drops below 3.6x). The image-stage cell is larger in raw area than the numeral at every viewport (288x216 vs a numeral glyph box roughly 130-190px wide by 65-110px tall) and is not fought down to fix that: RULINGS.md's law-10 standing acceptance check is 'the focal element is measurably the LARGEST TEXT', scoped to text, and imagery is deliberately a separate channel (law 5) with its own diegetic justification. The numeral still reads first in practice because it sits alone in the masthead row (isolation), takes the surface's one heavy-bracket treatment (see Chrome), and never changes within a scene (the image cell visibly swaps per beat, which is itself a cue that it is the secondary, updating channel rather than the anchor).

## Zones, glyph budgets, fluid rules

Container: `.ml-eva { container-type: inline-size; container-name: ml; }` wrapping the whole panel, one binary breakpoint at 700px of content inline-size (law 3), copied structurally from loadout-eva's `.lo-eva`/`@container lo (min-width: 700px)` pattern. Two rows only:

**Row 1, `.ml-mast` (masthead, full width, PERSISTENT across every beat within a scene, does not remount or re-animate on beat-to-beat clicks, only on scene mount):**
- Left stack: eyebrow (`.ml-eyebrow`, Silkscreen, --ml-fs-label: clamp(9px, calc(0.6cqi + 8px), 11px) copied verbatim from loadout's --lo-fs-label, color --r-note, letter-spacing 0.18em, budget <=32 chars, e.g. 'MORNING.LOG // DAY START' at 24 chars or 'SHOPFRONT.EXE // COUNTER SCENE' at 31), then the numeral row: a unit label ('DAY' or 'RUN' or a scenario-specific word, --r-note, --ml-fs-label, budget <=4 chars) beside the giant numeral (`.ml-num`, Silkscreen, --ml-fs-num as above, color --r-data, tabular-nums, budget exactly 2 glyphs for a zero-padded day/run index, or up to 4 glyphs for the rare system-word fallback documented below). The whole numeral block carries the ONE heavy corner-bracket treatment on this surface (24px leg / 4px --r-hazard border, copied verbatim from loadout-eva's `.lo-bracket` CSS, renamed `.ml-bracket`), per law 4's rule that the bracket flourish is scoped to the focal panel only.
- Right stack, inline: the register/status chip (`.ml-regchip`, structurally `.kp-chip-pct` from system.css: label auto-prefixed '// ' via the shared ::before, budget <=10 chars label / <=7 chars value) and the beat-progress dots (`.ml-beatdots`, budget 5 dots max, covering the largest scenario built here at 4). See 'Register chip and the one alarm state' for its two colour states.
- `.ml-mast` panel: 1px --r-struct hairline border (the panel edge itself, not the bracket), background a 3-4% --r-line-on-void tint matching the system's boxed-panel convention, padding ~10px.

**Row 2, `.ml-body` (two-column grid, `grid-template-columns: 288px 1fr`, FIXED height across every beat and every scenario: `min-height: 300px` flat, not fluid, not content-derived) -- this is the equal-footprint mechanism, see below:**
- Left column, `.ml-stage`: the image-stage cell, exactly 288x216px, 1:1 pixel mapping (never resized in CSS), border 2px --r-struct, background --px-void. Vertically centered within the 300px row (leaves ~42px of slack top and bottom; reads as instrument-panel breathing room, not a mistake, matching the precedent loadout-eva accepted for its own trinity's dead space). `data-fill="counter|backroom|standby"` selects which content the box shows; see 'Image stage' below.
- Right column, `.ml-text`: the text panel, 1px --r-struct hairline border, padding ~14-16px, `min-height: 100%` matched to the row. Contents, top to bottom: the speaker name chip (`.ml-name`, a small boxed `// LABEL` in --r-note text on a --r-struct 2px border box, NOT an inverse-video fill, budget <=6 chars matching SPEAKER_NAME exactly: RHEA, SYSTEM, DAD, ???), the beat's lines (`.ml-lines` > `.ml-line` per array entry, VT323, --ml-fs-body as above, color --r-line, line-height 1.3, no hard character cap per line since the row height is sized to the transcribed set's worst case, see 'Text panel sizing' below), then the NEXT/CONTINUE control pinned bottom-right via `justify-content: space-between` on a column flex container (`.ml-next`, see 'Beat choreography').

No footer row. An earlier draft gave the pointer/CTA its own row and cost ~50-56px for no new information once the beat-progress dots already live in the masthead and the CTA folds into the text panel's own bottom edge; applying loadout-eva's own lesson ('a row you do not share is a row you pay for in full') removed it before it was ever built.

**Narrow tier (<700px, tiling fallback only, no supported viewport reaches it):** `.ml-body` drops to one column, image stage stacked above the text panel; the numeral's clamp floor still holds (76px minimum); no tab strip and no paging is needed here (unlike loadout's PROGRAMS/RIG split), because this surface has nowhere near loadout's content volume -- law 8 category 5 (paging/tabs) is explicitly not invoked.

## The eight role tokens, each named once

- `--r-struct`: chrome -- window edge is NOT this (see hazard below), but the masthead panel border, the text-panel hairline, the image-stage frame, the beat-dot outlines (inactive), and the name-chip box border.
- `--r-note`: annotation that names, never states -- the eyebrow, the numeral's unit label (DAY/RUN), the register chip's label text, the speaker name chip's text.
- `--r-line`: live data -- the beat's spoken/system body copy itself. Chosen deliberately over --r-data (reserved below) and over inventing a color split between system and character speech: the transcribed copy already differentiates system voice from character voice typographically (system lines are ALL CAPS in story.ts, character lines are natural mixed case), so a second color channel for the same distinction would be redundant. The filled beat-progress dot (current position) also takes --r-line, since it is literally a live position readout.
- `--r-data`: the focal numeral ONLY, per the brief's explicit constraint. Not reused anywhere else on this surface.
- `--r-ok`: NOMINAL. Two uses, one meaning: the register/back-room status chip in its normal state (REGISTER: OPEN / BACK ROOM: SEALED), and the NEXT/CONTINUE control once the current beat has finished typing (it is 'ready', matching --r-ok's stated meaning exactly, mirroring loadout's `.lo-slab.is-ready` idiom).
- `--r-warn`: RISK, arms in exactly one built state (see 'Register chip and the one alarm state'). Not present anywhere on the DAY 1, DAY 5, or RUN 2 OPENER scenarios; a surface with no alarm has no --r-warn, and two of the four built scenarios prove that directly.
- `--r-aux`: the image-stage cell's live content, whichever camera is currently framed (counter or back room), per the FEED variation's ink-tint/true-1-bit/full-colour switch. Not applied to the standby/no-signal fill, since there is no camera signal to tint there.
- `--r-hazard`: structural red -- the window's outer edge/frame (`.term { border: 3px solid var(--r-hazard) }`, copied verbatim from loadout-eva's `.term` rule), the numeral's corner brackets, and the image-stage CAM tag's REC-style live dot (see 'Image stage').

## Image stage: one cell, three fills, and why the mapping is keyed on the DATA not the speaker

The fixed 288x216 `.ml-stage` cell is diegetically the shop's own camera system (two mounted cameras, per the Orchestrator's steer): CAM 1 is the counter camera (Rhea), CAM 2 is the back room camera (the curtain and the padlocked machine). Content is selected by which optional field the current StoryBeat carries, NOT by who is speaking:

- `data-fill="counter"` when the beat has a `portrait` set (sister/father/companion all route here structurally, though in the four built scenarios only sister's portrait appears): shows morning-rhea-feed.png at native 288x216, tag reads 'CAM 1 // COUNTER' (--r-note), a --r-hazard REC dot pulses at the shipped `kp-cursor-blink 0.9s steps(2) infinite` cadence (reused, not reinvented) in the top-left corner.
- `data-fill="backroom"` when the beat has a `still` set, REGARDLESS of speaker: shows morning-backroom-still.png at native 288x216, tag reads 'CAM 2 // BACK ROOM' (--r-note), no REC dot (a held frame, not a live feed).
- `data-fill="standby"` when neither field is set (every system-only beat in the transcribed set): no image, a dim ambient dither/scanline texture fills the box (reuse the shared `.kp-fw-body::before` conic-dither recipe at 5% opacity against --px-void), tag reads 'STANDBY' in --r-struct (dimmer than the other two tags, since there is nothing live to annotate).

This mapping is the reason DAY 10's beat 2 (sister speaking, `still` set) shows CAM 2, not her face: the camera cuts to the thing she is talking about (the curtain, the padlock) rather than staying on her, which is a meaningful reading of the existing data model, not an arbitrary rule. It is also the whole equal-footprint mechanism for problem (b): every beat, regardless of shape, renders the identical 288x216x300-tall body row with one of exactly three fills, so clicking through a scene never changes the window's height. Build all three fills and check pixel-for-pixel identical row height across the four transcribed scenarios (acceptance).

## Register chip and the one alarm state

Structurally `.kp-chip-pct` (system.css, shared, unmodified) for the nominal case. Per scenario: dayOpenScene reads label REGISTER, value OPEN (--r-ok) on every built day except DAY 10; runOpenerScene reads label BACK ROOM, value SEALED (--r-ok), reusing the exact vocabulary DesktopIdle already uses for meta.machineOpened (screens.tsx), not inventing new terms.

DAY 10 is the one day-start state that genuinely arms an alarm, exactly as the brief predicted: the scene's own first line is 'NO TICKETS ON THE SPIKE. THE BACK ROOM SETTLES UP TODAY.' The register chip flips to label REGISTER, value CLOSED, and becomes `.ml-regchip.is-warn`: --r-warn text flooding inverse video (void-on-warn fill, the shipped danger idiom), PLUS motion, both required by law 1's 'colour is never the only channel'. Do not reuse `.kp-chip-crimson` as-is (it is a single-accent-era class with no motion channel); build a local `.ml-regchip.is-warn` that composites the same inverse-video fill on --r-warn and copies loadout-eva's `.lo-riskflash` technique verbatim (a --r-warn difference-blend plate over the chip, opacity-animated on a promoted layer, `1.2s steps(2) infinite`, NOT an animated background/box-shadow -- that measured 50ms p95 under CRT FLAT in loadout's own harness, the opacity/mix-blend-mode:difference version measured 9.3ms). Fires once, arming for the whole DAY 10 scene from beat 0 (the condition is already true in the first line), not progressively. `--r-warn` appears NOWHERE else on this surface: not on the body text, not on the image stage, not as decoration. Play `registerAlarm` (new sfx, below) once on scene mount when this state is entered; do not re-fire it per beat-advance within the same scene.

## Beat choreography

**Typewriter (the primary interaction, per the brief).** On beat mount, lines type in sequence (line 2 does not begin until line 1 finishes), each character revealed at 24ms/interval (roughly 42 chars/sec), with a ~90ms pause between lines. Text typing begins ~70ms after beat mount, letting the image-stage cross-fade (below) register fractionally first without the two feeling stacked. Two states per beat: `typing` (revealing) and `revealed` (fully shown). The NEXT/CONTINUE control (`.ml-next`) stays a dim/ghost --r-struct outline, label hidden or muted, while `typing`; once `revealed` it becomes a solid --r-ok control reading NEXT (or CONTINUE on the scene's last beat), matching --r-ok's 'ready' meaning. The pulsing three-bar next-glyph from the shipped version is folded into this control rather than kept as a separate element.

**Click behaviour (new, replaces the shipped single-stage advance).** The whole card remains one click target. Click while `typing`: snap all lines of the CURRENT beat to fully revealed immediately, cancel in-flight reveal animation, play `storySkip` (new sfx, below), do NOT advance the beat, do NOT play `story`. Click while `revealed`: advance to the next beat (or call onDone on the last beat), play `story` (shipped, unchanged params, ui bus, jitter 0.05) exactly as today. If the image-stage fill key (counter/backroom/standby) is about to change on this advance, ALSO play `camSwitch` (new sfx, below), layered with `story` (both are well under 150ms total, this is intentional layering, not clutter); do not play it if the fill key is unchanged, and never play it on the initial mount of beat 0 (that entrance is covered by the window's own open sound/motion, not by this surface).

**Masthead persistence.** The masthead (numeral, eyebrow, register chip, beat dots) sits OUTSIDE whatever remount boundary keys the per-beat body row (the shipped code keys `.kp-story-beat` by `beat`, causing an instant full re-render each click; keep that keying on `.ml-body` only, not on `.ml-mast`). The masthead plays its own settle-in (opacity+translateY, 160ms steps(4), reusing the shared `kp-fw-in`-style keyframe shape) exactly ONCE, on scene mount, never on beat-to-beat clicks and never on scenario switches within the demo rig (which are full remounts and get it fresh). This is a deliberate restraint call: MORNING.LOG is one of the highest-frequency surfaces in the game (every day open, every run open/end, up to several dozen visits across one save), so its chrome does not get a showy per-beat flourish the way a once-per-load panel like LOADOUT.CFG can afford one.

**Image-stage transition.** When the fill key changes between beats, cross-fade the cell's contents (opacity only, promoted layer, 140ms steps(4)) -- not translateX, to stay cheap and because a directional wipe would compete with the text panel's own motion. If the fill key is unchanged between two consecutive beats (e.g. two portrait beats in a row), do not retrigger anything: ambient chrome that has not actually changed does not animate (law 7).

**Reduced motion.** Every beat mounts already `revealed` (lines fully shown in one frame, no visible per-character reveal); the NEXT/CONTINUE control is immediately in its --r-ok ready state; the image-stage cross-fade collapses to an instant swap (no opacity animation); the DAY 10 alarm's `.lo-riskflash`-style blink collapses to the static full inverse-video flood (still colour-plus-inverse, just not moving, matching the shipped kp-danger-blink reduced-motion fallback); the REC dot stops blinking and shows solid. Sound is unaffected per law 7: `story` still fires on every advance, `registerAlarm` still fires once on the DAY 10 scene mount. `storySkip` structurally cannot fire under reduced motion, since there is no typing state left to interrupt -- this is a natural consequence of the collapse, not a special case to implement.

## Text panel sizing (why 300px is enough)

The transcribed set's worst case is RUN 2 OPENER beat 2 (a single 101-character line) and beat 3 (three lines, 67/54/56 characters). At the tightest supported text-column width (760px laptop window, content 732px, minus the 288px image stage minus a 12px gap = 432px, roughly 40 characters per VT323 line at 21px), beat 3 wraps to about 6 visual lines (2+2+2). At 1.3 line-height and 21px type that is roughly 164px, plus the name chip (~24px), a gap, and the NEXT control's own row (~40px), plus panel padding (~28px), totals roughly 264px -- comfortably inside the fixed 300px row with margin to spare. This was computed against the actual transcribed lines below, not assumed; if new dayOpenScene/runOpenerScene copy is ever authored longer than this set's worst line, re-check against the fixed 300px budget before shipping it (do not silently let it overflow -- no internal scrollbars, ever).

## Cuts taken against the 700px ceiling, in law 8's order

The honest finding: this surface did not need much cutting, because the shipped version was already lean (a name, one to three lines, a button) with min-height 380px growing to 384px+ for still beats. The real defect was the ABSENCE of a fixed footprint, not an excess of content, so the work here is mostly additive structure (a masthead, role tokens, a fixed image cell), not subtraction. Walking law 8's categories honestly:

1. Decorative imagery that cannot survive its size: not invoked as a removal. The shipped still WAS shown oversized (576x384, sometimes downscaled from a 316x212 source into a larger box, a genuine v3 violation) and IS reduced in footprint here, to 288x216 -- but via CROP (law 5's mechanism: to show less, crop), not via shrinking into noise, since a tight security-camera-style crop reads fine at this size where a naive downscale of the full establishing shot would not.
2. Prose taught elsewhere: not applicable. Nothing on this surface is a mechanic description; there is no pointer sentence to write.
3. Always-visible descriptions to popups: not applicable, no secondary descriptions exist here.
4. Box treatment on lowest-priority data: applied proactively (not un-boxing something that was boxed, but designing it unboxed from the start, applying loadout-eva's own lesson before hitting the same wall): the beat-progress dots carry no border box at all, and the register chip's underlying `.kp-chip-pct` is already the system's lightest boxed treatment.
5. Paging/tabs in the narrow tier only: not needed even in the narrow (<700px, unreviewed) fallback -- this surface has nowhere near LOADOUT's content volume.

Estimated total window height at the WIDE tier (title bar 44px + term-body padding 24px + masthead ~108-130px depending on viewport + 10px gap + body row 300px, plus borders): roughly 490-510px across all three supported viewports, well inside the 700px target with margin left over deliberately, not from padding it out -- a two-row dialogue surface does not need to spend the same budget a three-panel instrument trinity does, and the remaining desk space is left for tiling exactly as loadout-eva's 'FREE DESK' ghost makes literal. Confirm the real number with the CDP harness at build time; these are pre-build estimates from the stated clamp() formulas, not measurements.

## How the other five callers land (documented, not built this cycle)

Only dayOpenScene passes StoryScene a `tag` today (shop-os.tsx line ~319, `tag={\`DAY ${run.day}\`}`); the other five pass none, so the masthead's numeral/unit-label pairing needs a value for each even though none currently exists in the shipped call sites. Extending `tag`-equivalent data per caller is a small integration-time change (a prop, not a new mechanic), suggested here so the panel never renders an empty focal slot:

- runOpenerScene(n) / runEndScene(n): eyebrow 'SHOPFRONT.EXE // COUNTER SCENE' (opener, built) or '// RUN END' (end, not built), unit RUN, numeral zero-padded n. Register chip BACK ROOM / SEALED for the opener (built); runEndScene's own first beat is always a literal strain-zero alarm ('NEURAL STRAIN: ZERO. CONNECTION SEVERED.'), which is a second, equally legitimate candidate for the --r-warn treatment this spec built for DAY 10 -- flagged for the Orchestrator's consideration at integration, not built here (out of this cycle's SCENARIO list).
- finaleWinScene(): eyebrow 'SHOPFRONT.EXE // CORE REACHED', unit CORE, and since there is no natural number, the numeral slot shows a short system WORD at the same --ml-fs-num scale instead of digits: OPEN. Register chip BACK ROOM / OPEN (--r-ok, nominal now that the lock has released). A strong, cheap payoff beat if built later.
- tutorialIntroScene() / tutorialOutroScene(): no day/run context exists pre-run-1. Suggested unit SYS, numeral-slot word BOOT (intro) / SEAL (outro), register chip SYSTEM / OVERRIDE (intro) / SYSTEM / SEALED (outro).

## Transcribed copy for the four built scenarios (verbatim from game/content/story.ts; do not alter a character)

SPEAKER_NAME map (screens.tsx): sister -> RHEA, father -> DAD, system -> SYSTEM, companion -> ???. Image-stage fill per beat is derived per 'Image stage' above (portrait -> counter, still -> backroom, neither -> standby).

## Chrome, schemes, CRT

Copy verbatim from loadout-eva/index.html rather than re-deriving: the full role-token block including both `:root[data-scheme="nerv"]` and `:root[data-scheme="tokyo"]` blocks with `--r-ok-glow`/`--r-warn-glow`; the `.term`/`.term-bar`/`.term-body` window-frame scaffolding; the `.lo-stage`/`.lo-warp`/`.lo-glass` CRT rig (all six glass layers, FLAT and OFF modes only, no CURVED, per RULINGS law 6); the `.lo-fit`/`.lo-fitwrap` true-resolution-scaled-to-fit stage technique so container queries see the real window width at every zoom. Window title bar text is scenario-driven: 'MORNING.LOG' for the three dayOpenScene scenarios, 'SHOPFRONT.EXE' for RUN 2 OPENER, matching shop-os.tsx's existing per-screen title switch exactly.

## USER RULING 2026-08-01, supersedes this spec's FEED default

Review verdict on the demo: "Love. Go with full color images for this one." FULL COLOUR is the default treatment for MORNING.LOG's camera cell, not INK TINT. INK TINT and TRUE 1-BIT remain available options. Integration must carry this default.

Consequence the spec did not anticipate: --r-aux was assigned to the ink tint, which full colour removes, so the role would have gone unpainted in the default state. It is reassigned to the camera cell's FRAME and CAM tag, which holds under every treatment and is the truer reading of the role (the camera is a different signal class whatever its picture looks like). STANDBY does not take the aux frame: a dead channel is not a channel. Re-verified, all eight roles paint under both schemes.
acceptance: At every one of the three supported viewports (16:9 1366x768 at window width 860px, 21:9 2560x1080 at 940px, 1280x800 laptop at 760px), the numeral resolves to the largest TEXT on the surface and is at least 3x the 21px body-copy cap (computed: 3.62x-4.33x across the three), clearing the law-2 2x minimum with margin
The body copy (.ml-line) never renders below 19px and never above 21px at any supported viewport, confirmed against --ml-fs-body's clamp()

The .ml-body row height is pixel-identical (within 1px) across all four transcribed scenarios and across all four beat shapes present in them (system/standby, sister/counter, system/backroom, sister/backroom), so clicking through any built scene never changes the window's total height

Window total height stays at or under 700px at every supported viewport across all four scenarios (target), and never exceeds 820px (absolute ceiling), measured with the CRT set to OFF per the law-10 measurement discipline
No internal scrollbar appears at any supported viewport x scenario combination
No border-radius appears anywhere except the CRT bezel/glass layers when CRT is FLAT

The image-stage asset renders at native 288x216 with no CSS scaling in either direction (computed element width equals natural asset width), for both morning-rhea-feed.png and morning-backroom-still.png

All eight role tokens (--r-struct, --r-note, --r-line, --r-data, --r-ok, --r-warn, --r-aux, --r-hazard) resolve to eight visually distinct colours under both data-scheme="nerv" and data-scheme="tokyo", and every one is used somewhere on the surface (no unassigned token)
