REPAIR.LOG rebuilt as a KP/OS v3 instrument panel at ui-demos/repair-log-v3/index.html, standalone (links ../_shared/kp.css + ../_shared/system.css + the Silkscreen/VT323/IBM-Plex-Mono stack, vanilla JS, no framework), following the loadout-eva build recipe verbatim: the role-token block, the six-layer FLAT/OFF glass, the real-resolution scaled stage rig, and the typeIn/countUpNode/later choreography helpers are ported class-for-class from ui-demos/loadout-eva/index.html rather than re-derived. Window chrome keeps the .term/.term-bar/.term-body naming, 3px var(--r-hazard) border (loadout used --r-hazard for the same edge), the 9px/26px drop-shadow, solid-ink title bar reading REPAIR.LOG.

GLANCE-ORDER ARGUMENT (the one design call this page makes on its own account, per its own header comment, lines 19-29): RULINGS.md's panel queue note ('the verdict is the obvious focal element') is OVERRULED. run-reducer.ts's `duelFinished` case routes a loss to screen 'runEnd' with lastResult null, and the finale win to 'finaleWin' (kernel-panic-site/app/src/game/run-reducer.ts, the block setting `lastResult: { won: true, ... }` under the ordinary win path, lines ~416-417 of report.tsx's own import chain confirm `lastResult.won` is never false in practice). REPAIR.LOG therefore only ever renders on a win, so the literal string 'REPAIR LOGGED' is INVARIANT on this surface and carries zero information ticket to ticket. A constant cannot be a defensible focal element under law 2 ('one focal element... the largest element' must be the thing worth looking at first). What varies is the transaction: what the ticket credited and what it billed in strain. So THE BILL, not the verdict, is focal, and the verdict is demoted to masthead-slab scale. I agree with this reasoning; it is the same conclusion I had independently reached from the same source fact before this rewrite request arrived, and I would have made the identical call.

glanceOrder.1st_focal: THE BILL (grid-area `bill`, zone Z3): a three-cell row, `.rl-cell` x3 inside `.rl-bill`, built by `buildBill()`. Cell 1 `// CREDITED` (the ticket's credited total, `.rl-num`, unit `CR`, itemized `payRows` receipt below). Cell 2 `// BILLED` (this ticket's strain cost, `.rl-num`, unit `STRAIN` or blank when clean, itemized `chipRows` receipt, the strain-left meter and 'STRAIN LEFT' foot readout, and the ONLY owner of --r-warn on the page). Cell 3 `// [piece head]` (what the ticket recovered: a `PatchGlyph` at 46px standing in for a third numeral, noun, status pill, typed flavour line). All three share `.rl-bracket` heavy hazard corner brackets, scoped to exactly these three cells and nowhere else on the page, per law 4. This mirrors LOADOUT.CFG's own precedent of a MULTI-numeral focal GROUP (the SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND trinity, three hero numerals named collectively as loadout-eva's '1st'), not a single number; I read this as the correct application of the same idiom, not a deviation from it.
glanceOrder.2nd: THE CACHE (grid-area `cache`, zone Z5): the AUGMENT CACHE draft, `.rl-div` hazard-stripe header with a live PICK ONE / INSTALLED / DRY state tag, then either 3 `.rl-card` draft cards, the `.rl-dry` message, or the `.rl-swap` EJECT panel. Ranked 2nd because it is the one thing on the surface the player must act on; the built page's own rig caption states this explicitly ('the AUGMENT CACHE, which is the only thing here that needs a hand').
glanceOrder.3rd: THE MASTHEAD (grid-area `mast`, zone Z1): the verdict slab 'REPAIR LOGGED' at `--rl-fs-slab` (clamp(22px, 3.4cqi, 32px)), always nominal (`--r-ok`), plus the client's typed win-line quote (`.rl-quote`, the one line of human voice on an instrumentation page) and the CLIENT/DEVICE chips. Present and legible, never extreme scale, because it is confirmatory chrome for an outcome that is never in doubt on this screen.
glanceOrder.4th: THE TRACE (grid-area `trace`, zone Z4): the ECG strain trace (`.rl-scope`, the surface's signature readout, one clean SVG grid + polyline + hazard trap-round tick marks) with the dive log (`.rl-log`, 2 columns, capped at 8 lines) sitting directly under the trace it annotates, both at support/body scale.
glanceOrder.ambient: the CLIENT CAM (grid-area `gutter`, zone Z2's `.rl-cam`, the diegetic shop-camera photo, `--r-aux`) and the four telemetry ticks plus the PATCH POUCH strip that share the gutter column with it. Deliberately never competing: the gutter never gets a container of its own scale ramp beyond the tick/label floors.

roleTokens.r-struct: the CLIENT CAM bezel border only (`.rl-cam{border:2px solid var(--r-struct);}`). General panel hairlines (`.rl-cell`, `.rl-scope`, `.rl-foot`) use the pre-existing `--ch-faint`/`--ch-dim` derived tones instead, which still recolour per scheme because `--ch` itself is redefined by `data-scheme`. This is not an inconsistency: it matches loadout-eva's own identically narrow application of `--r-struct` to `.lo-mon`'s bezel alone, with `.lo-panel` also on `--ch-faint`.
roleTokens.r-note: naming-only annotation: the masthead eyebrow, the CR/STRAIN unit captions, the four gutter tick labels, the 'CLIENT CAM' spine, the patch-piece noun (STRAIGHT/ELBOW/TEE/CROSS), the draft-card kind tags (BOOST/CONFIG), and the 'STRAIN LEFT' foot label until the alarm overrides it. It does NOT reach the bill cells' own `// CREDITED` / `// BILLED` / `// [piece head]` name labels (`.rl-cname{color:var(--ch);}`, plain base ink) -- that matches loadout-eva's `.lo-pname{color:var(--ch);}` precedent (a panel's own identifying name is chrome-weight, not annotation-weight), but it means the file's own header-comment line 39 ('note owns... the // prefixes') overclaims slightly against its own CSS. Harmless (the CSS is right, matching the reference build); worth tightening the comment's wording, not the rule.
roleTokens.r-line: live data: the ECG polyline stroke, every receipt row's numeric value (`.rl-receipt li em{color:var(--r-line);}`), the strain-left meter's lit segments outside the alarm band, the pouch-glyph arms via the shared `.kp-pp-arm` vocabulary, and the footer battery pips.
roleTokens.r-data: the two BILL hero numerals (CREDITED, BILLED) and nothing else (`.rl-num{color:var(--r-data);}`), overridden to `--r-ok` on the BILLED cell's CLEAN word-state and to `--r-warn` in the risk band. This widens RULINGS' original 'the focal numeral' (singular) to 'the two hero numerals' of the compound bill row, matching the pivot to a paired focal group; I agree with this reading rather than flagging it.
roleTokens.r-ok: NOMINAL: the verdict slab (always, since a loss never reaches this screen), the BILLED cell's CLEAN state, the picked draft card's border + reticle corner-ticks (`.rl-card.picked`) + its `.rl-stamp` INSTALLED badge, the fresh pouch slot, the RECOVERED piece's uncapped BANKED status pill, the strain-left meter's nominal band (>70), and the AUGMENT CACHE header's live 'PICK ONE' state tag specifically -- the SAME tag dims to `--ch-dim` once resolved to INSTALLED or DRY (`state.className = picked ? 'done' : ''`), so r-ok here marks 'this decision is open and awaiting you', the same 'live/ready' reading loadout-eva's own `.lo-slab.is-ready` used, not 'you already succeeded'.
roleTokens.r-warn: risk, exactly one owner: the BILLED cell's strain-LEFT reading, armed at `run.strain <= 35` (`RISK_BAND = 35`, the identical band LOADOUT.CFG uses, so the number means one thing across the desktop). Channels beyond colour: inverse video (`.rl-cell.is-risk .rl-num{background:var(--r-warn);color:var(--px-void);}`), a composited difference-blend blink on a promoted layer (`.rl-riskflash`, `rl-risk-blink 1.2s steps(2) infinite`, matching the exact idiom and cadence loadout-eva measured at 9.3ms p95), and the strain-left meter's own segment count as a position signal that survives a colourblind reader with the colour channel removed entirely. That is four channels total against the law's minimum of two. Nothing else on the surface ever takes it: the capped-bill receipt row, the LEFT ON THE BENCH status, trap markers on the trace, and the lost pouch slot all take --r-hazard instead, confirmed in the CSS, not just asserted in the header comment.
roleTokens.r-aux: the CLIENT CAM's own imagery: the ink-tint overlay (`.rl-cam .tint`, multiply-blended onto the 1-bit dither) and the bottom `.rl-camtag` caption pill (e.g. 'ON THE GOOD LIST', 'TILL RESTORED'). The top-left REC pip stays `--r-hazard` (matching loadout-eva's own REC treatment): a deliberate split between 'this is the imagery's own signal class' (aux) and 'this is generic recording-light chrome, identical on every camera in the OS' (hazard).
roleTokens.r-hazard: structural red: the window's own 3px edge, the heavy corner brackets on exactly the three THE BILL cells (all three, correctly, since together they ARE the one focal group -- not a partial/inconsistent application), the AUGMENT CACHE zone-boundary stripe (`.rl-div i`), the CLIENT CAM's REC pip, hazard tick marks on the ECG trace at every trap round (`.rl-scope line.trap`), the capped-bill inverse receipt row, the LEFT ON THE BENCH piece-status pill, and the lost pouch slot's dashed border and glyph tint.

fluid.containers: `.rl-wrap` (wraps `.rl-grid`, `container-type:inline-size;container-name:rl;`) drives the one binary breakpoint at 700px per law 3. Each `.rl-cell` (all three bill cells) additionally sets its own `container-type:inline-size`, so `.rl-num`'s cqi resolves against ITS OWN cell width, not the window's, matching loadout-eva's `.lo-panel` precedent exactly.
fluid.typeRamp: all defined once on `.rl-grid` and consumed everywhere below it (cqi in a custom property resolves at the use site, per RULINGS' documented gotcha, so a receipt row inside a `.rl-cell` container lands at a different absolute size than the masthead quote even though both reference `--rl-fs-body`): `--rl-fs-body: clamp(19px, calc(1cqi + 17px), 21px)` (VT323 floor, exact), `--rl-fs-label: clamp(9px, calc(0.6cqi + 8px), 11px)` (Silkscreen floor, exact), `--rl-fs-pill: clamp(9px, calc(0.5cqi + 8.5px), 10.5px)`, `--rl-fs-slab: clamp(22px, 3.4cqi, 32px)`, `--rl-fs-tickl: clamp(8px, calc(0.4cqi + 7.5px), 9px)`, `--rl-fs-tickv: clamp(12px, calc(0.8cqi + 10px), 14px)`, `--rl-fs-log: clamp(15px, calc(0.7cqi + 13px), 17px)` (receipt rows, dive-log lines, and the piece flavour line all share this one). The bill hero numeral is `clamp(44px, 26cqi, 78px)` inside its own `.rl-cell` container; the CLEAN word-state swaps to the smaller `clamp(30px, 17cqi, 52px)`.
fluid.breakpoint: `@container rl (min-width: 700px)` is the WIDE tier: `.rl-grid{grid-template-columns:190px 1fr; grid-template-areas:"mast mast" "gutter bill" "gutter trace" "cache cache" "foot foot";}`, the gutter beside bill+trace (never its own row: a 234px camera cell next to two short zones is free height, matching the 'a row you do not share is a row you pay for in full' lesson), `.rl-bill{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1.15fr;}` (the piece cell runs slightly wider than the two numeral cells), `.rl-log{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;}`, `.rl-draft{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);}`. A second, tighter rule at `@container rl (min-width:700px) and (max-width:800px)` (the 790px laptop window's ~760px content box) narrows the gutter to 176px, crops the CLIENT CAM to 162x186 (a CROP of the same 1:1 print, never a downscale, per law 5), and tightens cell/card padding. Below 700px (a tiling fallback only; none of the three supported viewports reach it) `.rl-grid[data-tab]` pages between a THE TICKET tab (bill+cache) and a THE DIVE tab (gutter+trace) behind `.rl-tabs`, with the masthead persistent above both.
fluid.measuredViewports: 16:9 term width 900px, 21:9 980px, laptop 1280x800 term width 790px; all three resolve `VP.win - 32 >= 700` in the rig's own `measure()` function, i.e. all three land WIDE and render the identical arrangement, satisfying law 3's supported-viewport requirement.

flaggedConcerns.concern: computed focal-to-second-largest ratio falls short of law 2's stated 2.2x benchmark
flaggedConcerns.detail: Working the actual clamp() values against the actual grid math (not measured live; I have no CDP/Bash access this session) at 16:9 (900px term): the bill row's content column is ~669px, so a CREDITED/BILLED cell is ~207px wide after the 1fr/1fr/1.15fr split, and `clamp(44px,26cqi,78px)` resolves to ~54px there, not the 78px ceiling. The masthead slab's `clamp(22px,3.4cqi,32px)` resolves against the full ~870px content width (it is not inside its own container), landing at its 32px ceiling. Ratio: ~54/32 = 1.7x. At 21:9 (980px term) I get ~60/32 = 1.9x. At the laptop's tight-end breakpoint (790px term, narrower gutter and cell padding) I get ~46/26 = 1.8x. All three clear the law's explicit FAILURE case ('1.3x... has no hierarchy') with real margin, but all three fall short of the reference build's own achieved 2.2x. Recommend shrinking `--rl-fs-slab`'s ceiling (e.g. to ~26px) rather than growing the bill numeral further into its already-narrow third-of-a-row cell: the demo's own argument is that the verdict is DELIBERATELY subordinate, so a smaller slab both closes the ratio gap and reinforces the argument being made. Flagging with the arithmetic shown rather than asserting a fix, since I have not measured the live page; recommend a CDP pass before sign-off.

But `content/customers.ts` gives Bram Hollander `tiers: [2, 3]` (id `bram-hollander`), and `content/arc.ts`'s day 8 config caps `jobTiers` at `[4, 4, 4]` (no day offers tier 5 until day 9, and even then only as the last slot). The win line and figure art are correctly verbatim (`bram-hollander`'s own shipped `winLine` and device), so nothing here invents fiction; it is a transcription slip in the numbers only. Recommend either dropping to a tier Bram's data supports (tier 3: `40+25*3=115`, still leaves room for the 40-cap chip bill to read as a close call) or, if the higher pay is wanted for scenario variety, swapping to a customer whose `tiers` actually reach 5.

flaggedConcerns.concern: the 'no piece this ticket' empty branch is neither exercised by a scenario nor defensively handled in code
flaggedConcerns.detail: report.tsx's own poster logic has three branches: cleanRun banked, patchDrop (banked or capped), and a genuine null/null case rendering 'NO PIECE THIS TICKET' with the pointer line 'Nothing came off this one. Recommend making the piece-cell builder defensive against `S.piece === null` (rendering the verbatim NO PIECE THIS TICKET / pointer-line pair inside the same fixed-footprint cell) even if no SCENARIO button is added to demonstrate it live this cycle.

items.spec:
MANUAL.TXT rebuilt as a KP/OS v3 instrument panel at ui-demos/manual-v3/index.html, standalone (links ../_shared/kp.css + ../_shared/system.css + the Silkscreen/VT323/IBM-Plex-Mono Google Fonts stack, vanilla JS, no framework), following the loadout-eva build recipe verbatim per RULINGS.md law 9: the role-token block (:root defaults plus data-scheme="nerv"/"tokyo", copied from ui-demos/loadout-eva/index.html lines 78-141, not retyped), the six-layer FLAT/OFF glass (.lo-glass and its g-scan/g-mask/g-bloom/g-spec/g-vig/g-bezel children, no CURVED per law 6), and the load-choreography helpers (typeIn-style typewriter, kp-slot-in stagger, kp-page-flip transition) are ported class-for-class rather than re-derived. Structure and copy are read from the CURRENT working-tree kernel-panic-site/app/src/components/os/windows/manual.tsx (its five-tab shape, its Ability sub-component, its verbatim strings, corrected 2026-08-31 to split-board rules, built from this file and not from memory) and kernel-panic-site/app/src/game/content/kit.ts (AUGMENTS, all 18 entries; ATTACK_MODE_LABEL/DEFEND_MODE_LABEL; attackModeDesc/defendModeDesc/scanDesc at tier 1, matching the shipped component's own tier-1 call) and patch-cells.ts (PATCH_POUCH_MAX). All player-facing copy is transcribed verbatim; nothing is reworded.

HEADLINE DECISIONS, in the order they drove the design:

1. FOCAL ELEMENT: the active section's own HERO LETTERHEAD (DIVE / KIT / PATCHES / AUGMENTS / BAYS), at extreme scale against body text. This generalizes DAD.LOG's own resolved question (dadlog-v3/NOTES.md: 'a reading surface looks like it has no focal element, which is the trap... the title is the answer, because it is the one thing on the page that says WHICH ARTIFACT THIS IS') to a five-page reference document: the hero says WHICH PAGE OF THE MANUAL YOU ARE ON, which is the one fact every other element on the surface is subordinate to. The shipped component already isolates this exact string via its own Hero component (manual.tsx:188); this spec keeps that instinct and gives it the scale law 2 asks for.

2. TWO SEPARATE NAVIGATIONS, kept distinct rather than merged. The TAB STRIP (5 named, directly clickable buttons) is the primary way to reach a section, reskinned but functionally unchanged from the shipped component. The FOOTER (PREV/NEXT ghost buttons plus a PAGE n/5 chip) is kept as a secondary, book-flipping affordance over the same five sections, also functionally unchanged from shipped. A THIRD, new control exists only on the AUGMENTS tab: an in-frame SET n/N pager (see augmentsPaging) that steps through that page's own card sets. The three never collapse into one control: PAGE counts sections, SET counts card sets within one section, and conflating them would make 'PAGE 2' ambiguous between 'the KIT tab' and 'the second card set of AUGMENTS'.

3. THE HARD CASE, AUGMENTS' 18 cards. RULINGS.md law 8 step 5 reads 'Paging or tabs in the narrow tier only', which governs not reaching for pagination as a shortcut around a WIDE-tier cutting problem a real cut would solve. It does not govern this case: 18 full-text catalog entries cannot render on one page at any viewport under the height ceiling, at any card density, so the SET pager is structural content representation, not a cut-order fallback, exactly the argument DAD.LOG's own NOTES.md already settled for its document reader ('Paging is structural, not a fallback... it is the thing that makes the no-scrollbar law true for content it has never seen'). The mechanism is DAD.LOG's own measure-then-pack paginator (dadlog-v3/index.html's paginate()/showPage(), cited by name), generalized from prose blocks to whole ROWS of a 3-column card grid. See augmentsPaging for the anatomy, the mechanism and a worked estimate.

4. EQUAL FOOTPRINT ACROSS TABS. The window's outer height is IDENTICAL whether the open tab is DIVE (two short paragraphs) or AUGMENTS (a dense multi-card grid): the content frame is a fixed-height box (RULINGS law 4's equal-footprint rule, generalized here from empty/filled slots to short/dense TABS, matching NIGHT.SYS's 'the window stopped growing' and DAD.LOG's identical resolution). Short tabs leave visible dead space below their prose; per loadout-eva's own precedent this reads as instrument-panel spacing, an accepted cost, not an oversight.

5. THE PATCHES DIAGRAM IS CUT, not fixed. The shipped component renders /assets/px/window/solder-bench.png, a 304x304 native dither, at a CSS-forced 180x128 (manual.tsx:86-96), a live law 5 violation (browser-downscaled 1-bit art mushes into grey noise; see the suggestion item flagging this for other unconverted windows). Rather than re-cropping it correctly, this spec cuts it outright, for two reasons: it is the SAME bench asset LOADOUT.CFG and DAD.LOG already show, and putting a third instance of it on a third window is the exact decorative duplication NIGHT.SYS's NOTES.md already declined for the identical asset ('the SAME bench camera LOADOUT.CFG already owns; putting it on a second window in the same desktop is decorative duplication'); and MANUAL.TXT's own identity as a plain-text reference file is reinforced, not weakened, by staying purely typographic, a small diegetic point worth stating rather than assuming. The freed vertical room goes to PATCHES' own prose, otherwise the shortest page on the surface. Art budget for this study stays at literal zero: no new dither pass, no re-crop, nothing referenced.

6. KIT's ATTACK.EXE/DEFEND.EXE re-chunked, not shortened. The shipped component concatenates all three of ATTACK's (or DEFEND's) mode descriptions plus a closing sentence into one run-on paragraph (manual.tsx:69-78) built from attackModeDesc/defendModeDesc at tier 1; the words survive character for character here, just laid out as one labeled row per mode (REDIRECT / ARM: HALT / ARM: SIPHON, or PURGE / LOCK / WARD) inside the program's card, a definition-list reflow rather than a content cut. SCAN.EXE, already one sentence, is unchanged. The three program cards sit in a 3-column row on the KIT page, mirroring LOADOUT.CFG's own SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND trinity so a player who has configured one recognizes the other; a row shared by three short cards costs the height of one, not three, matching the reference build's own 'a row you do not share is a row you pay for in full' lesson run in the direction that pays for itself.

7. --r-warn and --r-aux go UNOWNED, decided rather than defaulted. MANUAL.TXT is read-only reference chrome: no live risk state (no strain, no timer, nothing that can fail while this window is open) and no diegetic camera moment (a manual page is not a live feed), so per law 1's own text ('If a surface has no alarm state, it has no --r-warn') and NIGHT.SYS's identical call on --r-aux, both roles are confirmed unreferenced anywhere in this surface's CSS, not merely unused by omission.

glanceOrder.1st_focal: the active section's HERO LETTERHEAD (.mn-hero, one of DIVE / KIT / PATCHES / AUGMENTS / BAYS), sized well past 2x the next-largest text at every supported viewport (see fluid.typeRamp). It is the only thing on the surface answering 'which page am I on', and every other element is legible support for it.
glanceOrder.2nd: the section's own content: for DIVE/KIT/PATCHES/BAYS a short prose block (KIT additionally carries the SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND trinity row); for AUGMENTS the current page's card set (see augmentsPaging). This is what the page actually says, and it is what the player came to read.
glanceOrder.3rd: the TAB STRIP (.mn-tabs): five directly-clickable named buttons, the active one carrying --r-ok inverse fill plus a corner-tick reticle. States which sections exist and which one is open, but never competes with the hero for first read.
glanceOrder.ambient: the FOOTER (PAGE n/5 chip plus PREV/NEXT), the AUGMENTS-only SET n/N pager, and every REQ footnote line. Deliberately smallest and lowest-contrast; a manual's page furniture, not its content.

roleTokens.r-struct: card and row hairlines (.mn-aug-card, .mn-augrow), inactive tab borders, the KIT trinity card outlines, and (narrow tier only) the dead-pager dashed chrome when a card set has only one page.
roleTokens.r-note: naming-only annotation: the TAG word (CONFIG/BOOST, rendered through text-transform: uppercase over the existing lowercase kind strings, matching .kp-datarow's own span treatment rather than retyping the copy), every REQ line ('// NEEDS <name>.' or '// NEEDS A PIECE IN THE POUCH.', built exactly as the shipped Ability component's req prop already computes it), the footer's '// PAGE _' and the in-frame '// SET _' label prefixes, and inactive tab labels.
roleTokens.r-line: live/filled data: the CONFIG-kind pip's fill (a filled kp-pip-sq marks a config augment, an outline one marks a boost, a second channel beyond the TAG word per law 1's 'colour is never the only channel'), and, under the DOTS pager variation, the current page's filled index square.
roleTokens.r-data: the section HERO letterhead, and, at a much smaller scale, every card/row NAME (matching DAD.LOG's identical rail-filename precedent: a title-weight role reused at multiple sizes is legal under law 2 as long as the FOCAL scale stays singular, which it does here by a wide margin, see fluid.typeRamp).
roleTokens.r-ok: the active tab (inverse fill plus corner-tick reticle), and nothing else: this surface has no purchase, no pick, no confirmable state beyond 'which page is open'.
roleTokens.r-warn: UNOWNED. No alarm state exists on this surface; confirmed unreferenced in every CSS rule.
roleTokens.r-aux: UNOWNED. No imagery exists on this surface (see spec point 5); confirmed unreferenced in every CSS rule.
roleTokens.r-hazard: structural red: the window's own 3px edge, the hazard-stripe divider between the tab strip and the content frame (the one zone boundary this surface has), and the content frame's corner brackets, scoped to that one focal zone per law 4.

augmentsPaging.cardAnatomy: NAME (.mn-aname, r-data, Silkscreen, --mn-fs-name) plus a leading kp-pip-sq (filled r-line for kind:"config", outline r-struct for kind:"boost") plus the TAG word (r-note) on the header row; DESC (.mn-adesc, plain body ink, VT323, --mn-fs-body, verbatim AugmentDef.desc, never truncated); an optional REQ line (.mn-areq, r-note) for the 3 of 18 entries carrying a requires clause (siphonPlus needs cfgArmSiphon, tripwire needs cfgArmHalt, patchRefund needs a pouch piece), built exactly as manual.tsx's own req prop logic already resolves it. No card gets corner brackets (law 4 reserves those for the one focal zone, which here is the content frame as a whole, not any individual card) and no card is interactive: reading is the only verb this page supports.
augmentsPaging.mechanism: measure-then-pack, generalizing dadlog-v3's paginate()/showPage() from prose blocks to whole grid ROWS. All 18 cards render off-screen (or in a zero-opacity measuring pass) at the live column width in AUGMENTS array order (kit.ts:188-304), grouped 3-per-row (6 rows total); each row's height is measured as the max of its 3 cards' natural heights; rows are then greedily packed into pages, accumulating running height until the next row would exceed the fixed content-frame budget, at which point a new page opens. A row is never split. Recomputes on resize/tier change, matching DAD.LOG's own resize-repaginate behaviour. The Orchestrator may reorder AUGMENTS for DISPLAY packing only (never reordering kit.ts itself) so the two longest descriptions do not both cluster onto early rows; this is an optional presentational technique, not a requirement.
augmentsPaging.workedEstimate: Not measured, no CDP/browser access this session; arithmetic shown so the Orchestrator's real pass can be checked against it, not asserted as fact. At an estimated 1040px window (matching DAD.LOG's own 16:9 footprint) the content box is roughly 998px, and a 3-column grid with 16px gaps yields a column near 322px. VT323 at this width runs roughly 27 to 30 characters per line. The two longest descriptions in the whole catalog are cfgArmSiphon's (kit.ts:201, roughly 173 characters) and cfgWard's (kit.ts:215, roughly 152 characters), and by array order they land in ROW 1 and ROW 2 respectively (kit.ts:189-216 is the four config augments, cfgArmHalt/cfgArmSiphon/cfgLock/cfgWard, filling exactly rows 1 and 2 of a 3-per-row grid). Each therefore drives its own row to roughly 6 to 7 wrapped lines of body text, an estimated 200 to 240px per row including the name row and card padding. Rows 3 through 6 (longArms through darkDiscount) run far shorter, mostly under 100 characters, an estimated 90 to 120px per row. Packed greedily against an estimated 440 to 480px content-frame budget, the likely outcome is 2 pages, front-loaded and uneven (something near a 6-card page 1 and a 12-card page 2, or a 9/9 split if the budget lands generously), never a clean guaranteed 9-and-9 split. State the real count from the CDP measurement, not this estimate, in the demo's NOTES.md. Full window height estimate follows the same honesty rule: title bar plus body padding plus tab strip plus divider plus a 440 to 480px content frame plus footer plus padding sums to roughly 640 to 660px, under the 700px target and consistent with every sibling panel's 650 to 731px range, but unverified.
augmentsPaging.setPager: .mn-cardpager: PREV/NEXT ghost buttons plus a 'SET n/N' chip (SET is a minted UI noun, not copy, parallel to DAD.LOG's PAGE/FILE nouns; it exists so this control is never confused with the footer's PAGE n/5, which counts sections, not card sets), living inside the content frame below the grid, never in the window footer. Hides its own buttons, not the chip, when the packer ever produces exactly one page, mirroring dl-pager's data-single convention (dadlog-v3/index.html:641) exactly.
augmentsPaging.compactListAlternative: the AUGMENTS LAYOUT variation's second option. Each augment becomes one .mn-augrow strip instead of a grid card: NAME in a fixed roughly 190px column, the kind pip plus TAG word beside it, DESC filling the remaining width, REQ trailing inline only when present. Rows are hairline-bordered top and bottom rather than fully boxed, closer to a spec sheet than a card deck. The same measure-then-pack mechanism applies at row granularity (no 3-per-row grouping, since a list row is already full width), and is expected to need fewer pages than CARD GRID because a short description never pays for a name/tag header row's own vertical weight twice.

cuts.item: the PATCHES tab's bench diagram (manual.tsx:86-96, /assets/px/window/solder-bench.png downscaled 304 to 180)
cuts.action: cut outright, not re-cropped
cuts.why: see spec point 5: it repeats the exact bench asset LOADOUT.CFG and DAD.LOG already show, and MANUAL.TXT's own plain-text identity is reinforced by staying typographic. This is the ONLY true content cut on this surface; everything else is reflow (KIT's re-chunking) or genuine pagination (AUGMENTS), not shrinkage.

fluid.containers: .mn-wrap (wraps the whole window content, container-type: inline-size; container-name: mn;) drives the one binary breakpoint at 700px per law 3. The AUGMENTS content frame additionally sets its own nested container-type: inline-size, so the grid's column math resolves against ITS width, matching loadout-eva's .lo-panel nested-container precedent, not the outer window's.
fluid.typeRamp: --mn-fs-hero: clamp(46px, 8cqi, 84px); --mn-fs-body: clamp(19px, calc(1cqi + 17px), 21px) (the VT323 floor, exact, matching loadout-eva's narrow-clamp technique for expressing a hard floor as a fluid rule); --mn-fs-label: clamp(9px, calc(0.6cqi + 8px), 11px) (Silkscreen tab labels, TAG words); --mn-fs-name: clamp(12px, calc(0.8cqi + 10px), 15px) (card/row NAME); --mn-fs-chip: clamp(9px, calc(0.5cqi + 8.5px), 10.5px) (PAGE/SET chip text). At the narrowest supported window (940px laptop target, roughly 760px inner content) the hero resolves near 61px against a 21px body ceiling, a 2.9x ratio; at the widest (1100px, 21:9) it resolves near its 84px ceiling against the same 21px, a 4x ratio. Both clear law 2's 2x bar with margin, unverified estimates pending the Orchestrator's CDP pass.
fluid.breakpoint: @container mn (min-width: 700px) is WIDE: the tab strip stays one row, five buttons, white-space: nowrap (matching DAD.LOG's own masthead lesson, 'everything in that row is now budgeted against the NARROWEST supported window'), and the AUGMENTS grid runs 3 columns. Below 700px, a tiling fallback only, no supported viewport reaches it: the tab strip wraps 3 plus 2, and the AUGMENTS grid drops to 2 columns.
fluid.measuredViewports: target frame widths, matching DAD.LOG's own measured footprint since both carry a comparable multi-column reference layout: 16:9 1366x768 window 1040px, 21:9 2560x1080 window 1100px, laptop 1280x800 window 940px. All three clear the 700px content-box breakpoint (window minus border and body padding), so all three render the identical WIDE arrangement per law 3; none of these numbers is authoritative until the Orchestrator's own CDP measurement replaces this estimate.

crt.layers: the six-layer glass (.lo-glass, g-scan/g-mask/g-bloom/g-spec/g-vig/g-bezel) copied verbatim from loadout-eva/index.html; no new layer, no CURVED mode per law 6.
crt.modes: FLAT (default) and OFF; OFF removes every layer outright rather than fading them, and the page must still read as a finished flat-ink print with none of its richness living in the CRT layer, matching every sibling panel's standing rule.

choreography.mount: on first load (default tab DIVE, matching the shipped component's own initial state) the tab strip slots in via the existing kp-slot-in keyframe (kp.css:206-210, reused verbatim), staggered left to right roughly 60ms apart; the hero types in via a per-element-scoped typewriter (law 7's 'scope typewriters per element' rule, so switching tabs later never restarts an unrelated element), roughly 24ms per character matching DAD.LOG's typeIn() cadence; the section body begins typing roughly 120ms after the hero starts.
choreography.tabSwitch: the content frame replays the existing kp-page-flip animation (system.css:151-158, 160ms steps(4), the exact class the shipped manual.tsx already toggles on its flip-keyed remount) and the new section's hero and body retype from empty, scoped to that remount only.
choreography.augmentsEntry: on first arriving at AUGMENTS (by tab click or by PREV/NEXT), the current page's cards or rows slot in via kp-slot-in staggered PER ROW, not per card, roughly 70ms between rows, settling within 250 to 300ms total, deliberately short and proportionate to this surface's density (matching NIGHT.SYS's identical reasoning for its own settle time).
choreography.setSwitch: changing the SET pager replays kp-page-flip on the content frame plus the row stagger for the new page's cards only; the tab strip and hero are untouched.
choreography.reducedMotion: hero and body render at full text in one frame; cards and rows appear without stagger; every page-flip transition becomes an instant swap; sound is unaffected, matching every sibling panel's rule verbatim.

sound.reused: pageFlip (already defined in audio.ts, already wired in the current manual.tsx via sfx("pageFlip", { bus: "ui" })) fires on every tab switch AND every AUGMENTS SET page change, since both are literally 'turn a page' on the same in-fiction object. No new preset.
sound.whyNothingElse: the brief's own framing holds: MANUAL.TXT is read-only reference chrome. Cards and rows are not clickable, draggable, or purchasable; nothing here confirms a choice or carries risk. Adding a hover-tick to the tab strip or a select-tick to a card would be feedback for an action with no consequence, which is exactly the unjustified addition this brief asked to be argued against. Zero sfx items are filed this cycle.

acceptance: at every supported viewport the active section's hero letterhead is measurably the largest text on the surface, at least 2x the next-largest element (card/row NAME), confirmed by computed font-size, not asserted
window height, measured with the CRT off, is IDENTICAL across all five tabs (DIVE, KIT, PATCHES, every AUGMENTS page, BAYS) at a given viewport, holding the equal-footprint law
no internal scrollbar renders anywhere on the surface at any tab, any AUGMENTS page, any AUGMENTS LAYOUT option, or any supported viewport

every one of the 18 augment entries renders its full name, tag, description and, if present, requirement line with zero truncation or ellipsis, across every AUGMENTS page and in both AUGMENTS LAYOUT options

the AUGMENTS SET pager's N always equals the number of pages the greedy row-packer actually produced for the current viewport and layout option, and recomputes correctly on a resize that crosses the 700px breakpoint
switching tabs or AUGMENTS SET pages plays the existing kp-page-flip animation (160ms steps(4)) and defines no new keyframe
no CSS rule on this surface ever resolves --r-warn or --r-aux; both are confirmed unreferenced

both NERV and TOKYO NIGHT resolve r-struct, r-note, r-line, r-data, r-ok and r-hazard to six visibly distinct values; a page with no data-scheme attribute collapses all eight roles onto the single accent, matching the :root default

all three supported viewports (16:9 1366x768, 21:9 2560x1080, laptop 1280x800) render the identical WIDE arrangement, one-row tab strip, 3-column AUGMENTS grid; none falls to the narrow tiling fallback
no border-radius appears anywhere except the CRT tube's own bezel; no em dash or en dash appears anywhere in rendered text
the PATCHES tab renders no img element anywhere in its DOM

under prefers-reduced-motion, every tab renders its settled state in one frame, full hero and body text, cards/rows present with no stagger, instant tab and SET transitions, with pageFlip's sound still firing on click, unaffected by the motion setting

every transcribed string (DIVE's two paragraphs, KIT's three program blocks including the per-mode re-chunking, PATCHES' three paragraphs, all 18 AUGMENTS name/desc/req fields, BAYS' two paragraphs plus its dim pointer line) matches kernel-panic-site/app/src/components/os/windows/manual.tsx and game/content/kit.ts verbatim, character for character

items.idea: Give each augment card/row and each KIT program card a stable DOM anchor (a data-aug-id or data-program attribute) plus a small openManual(section, anchorId) window-manager hook, so other windows' popups and tooltips can deep-link straight to the exact page and card instead of only naming it in prose. A future LOADOUT.CFG mode popup, for instance, could carry a trailing 'MORE: MANUAL > KIT > ARM: SIPHON' pointer that opens MANUAL.TXT pre-tabbed and pre-paged to that exact entry.
items.why: turns MANUAL.TXT from something the player has to flip through and hunt in into an actual cross-referenced index, and is exactly the kind of clearer-interface move the Tutorial Agent's charter prefers over adding another coachmark (CLAUDE.md: 'prefer a clearer interface (tier 0) over a coachmark'). Cheap to add now while the AUGMENTS grid and KIT trinity are being built fresh; expensive to retrofit once several other windows already reference MANUAL.TXT by name only.

items.idea: Audit the remaining shipped, still-unconverted window components, especially LEDGER (the other item in the law-11 queue), for the exact 1:1-imagery violation this cycle found and cut in MANUAL.TXT: an img rendered at its native intrinsic size in width/height but forced smaller via an inline CSS style, which resamples a 1-bit dither into grey noise. A quick grep across kernel-panic-site/app/src/components/os/windows/ for a style width/height pair that disagrees with its own width/height attributes would catch any other live instances before each gets individually rediscovered window by window.
items.why: law 5 ('1:1 pixel mapping, never downscaled... browser downscaling mushes the dots into grey noise') is being enforced case by case as each window converts to v3, which means it is easy for an instance to survive simply because its window has not come up for conversion yet.

A. THE TABLE-SHAPED QUESTION, ANSWERED FIRST. LEDGER is NOT open-ended like MANUAL's 18-card AUGMENTS catalog or DAD.LOG's growing journal: its row count is fixed by the component's own JSX, not by save-file growth. THIS RUN carries exactly 6 label/value rows (ATTEMPT, DAY, RAM / TURN, KIT TIERS, AUGMENTS, NEURAL STRAIN) plus one focal cell (CREDITS) plus two pip rows (POUCH, BAYS); LIFETIME carries exactly 6 rows (ATTEMPTS, MACHINE BEATEN, JOBS CLEARED, DIVES LOST, SCANS RUN, MOST USED MODE) plus one dossier cell (MOST LETHAL). Every value is a bounded string (a customer roster of 12, a fixed KIT TIERS format, a capped augment count) that can grow numerically but never grow ROWS. This reaffirms the kpos-window-sizing-law finding from the v2 pass ('LEDGER.LOG's ~16 rows... just needed a wider window and a smarter layout, not a paging mechanism') for v3: NO measure-then-pack SET pager is built here, unlike MANUAL.TXT's AUGMENTS tab. What IS reused from manual-v3/dadlog-v3 is the EQUAL-FOOTPRINT discipline (law 4), applied to run states rather than to pagination, per section E below. B. GLANCE ORDER (stated first per law 2, type scale built to enforce it). 1st: the THIS RUN CREDITS numeral, the surface's one focal element at extreme scale, `clamp(64px, 22cqi, 108px)` VT323 digits in `--r-data`, boxed in a `--r-hazard` corner-bracket + hairline frame (law 4's focal-panel chrome) with the shipped `Nodes` six-dot join decoration reskinned to `--r-struct`, a `--r-note` 'CREDITS' eyebrow above it and a `--r-note` 'cr' unit suffix riding the numeral's baseline (matching the shipped `cr` unit). 2nd: the masthead, `LEDGER \u2116{meta.runCount}` (verbatim, the shipped `\u2116` glyph preserved) in Silkscreen `clamp(22px, 4cqi, 34px)`, well under half the hero's floor, beside the BACK ROOM chip. Ratio check: 64/34 = 1.9x at the type floor, 108/22 = 4.9x at the ceiling; both clear law 2's 2.2x reference bar except the narrow floor case, which is flagged honestly below as the one clamp pairing the Orchestrator should re-check live (an estimate, not a CDP measurement; this agent has no browser access). 3rd: the THIS RUN rail (6 rows in `--r-note` labels / `--r-line` values, POUCH and BAYS as `PipRow`s beside the CREDITS cell) with NEURAL STRAIN as the surface's one alarm (see C). 4th: the LIFETIME rail below a `--r-hazard` hazard-stripe divider (reusing the shipped `Ruler` component's position, restyled from a plain rule to the 45deg hazard-stripe pattern law 4 names), beside the MOST LETHAL dossier cell (`--r-aux` ink-tinted portrait, see D). 5th, deliberately ambient, never competing: the footer print furniture (`LedgerFoot`, unchanged structurally) — dot-matrix ticks in `--r-line`, the seeded hex strip and 'KP/OS REPAIR BENCH v9.2' brand line in `--r-note`, the battery-pip glyph in `--r-struct`. C. THE ALARM: NEURAL STRAIN, and why LEDGER owns MORE roles than MANUAL.TXT. Unlike MANUAL.TXT (which left both `--r-warn` and `--r-aux` unowned, a reference/help surface with no live risk state and no imagery), LEDGER genuinely owns all eight roles: it shows a live run's CURRENT strain (a real risk readout) and a real dossier photo (MOST LETHAL). NEURAL STRAIN reuses the EXACT shipped risk band verbatim rather than inventing a new one: `run.strain > 70` -> `--r-ok` tint on the SegMeter fill and the `{run.strain}/100` numeral (nominal); `35 < run.strain <= 70` -> default `--r-line` (neutral, no role claim); `run.strain <= 35` -> `--r-warn`, the surface's ONE alarm, and ONLY this readout ever takes it. The alarm carries the same three channels REPAIR.LOG's v3 build already proved (report.tsx's own header comment): colour, inverse video, and motion, reusing loadout-eva's exact composited technique (`.lo-riskflash`/`lo-risk-blink`, a `mix-blend-mode:difference` plate on a promoted layer animating `opacity` at `1.2s steps(2) infinite`, never `background`/`box-shadow`) so the alarm never re-triggers the CRT glass's paint cost. Ambient `--r-hazard` chrome (the CREDITS panel's corner brackets, the window edge, the LIFETIME divider stripe) never animates, matching law 1's asymmetry rule exactly. `--r-ok` is ALSO owned a second way on this surface: the BACK ROOM chip flips between `--r-struct` dashed/dim (SEALED) and `--r-ok` filled inverse (OPEN), never `--r-data` or `--r-hazard`, since a boolean unlock flag is not a hero numeral and must not compete with CREDITS at the same visual weight (law 2's 'nothing ambient may compete' rule applied to a NEW chip, not just an existing one). D. MOST LETHAL: a REAL, CONFIRMED law-5 fix, not a new imagery case. Checked the shipped component directly as the brief asked: `ledger.tsx:155` renders `` inside `.kp-ledger2-lethal`, which `styles.css:5107` squashes with `.kp-ledger2-lethal .kp-cell img { max-height: 170px; }` (compounding the base `.kp-cell img` rule at `styles.css:2696-2705`: `width:100%; height:auto; max-height:210px; object-fit:cover`). This is TWO compounded lies about the same pixels: the width/height ATTRIBUTES (880x880) are already wrong for 3 of the 4 customers with card portraits, since `roster-art.ts`'s own comment says 'Card portraits (304px 1-bit; Dex's ratified look ships at 880px)' (CARD_PORTRAITS, roster-art.ts:13-19) — Juno/Sable/Aldous ship at 304x304, only Dex Marlowe ships at 880x880 — and then whichever real size is served gets CSS-downscaled to 170px regardless, a live instance of exactly the `law5-downscale-audit` pattern (this proposal's own prior item, filed against MANUAL.TXT, which named LEDGER as 'the next place to check'). FIX, reusing DIVE.EXE's already-shipped `deviceMacroFor` crop-window mechanism (roster-art.ts:117-127) instead of CSS max-height: the MOST LETHAL cell renders the customer's NATIVE portrait (304x304 for Juno/Sable/Aldous, 880x880 for Dex) inside a FIXED, smaller, `overflow:hidden` crop window, 1:1, never resampled, with `top`/`left` offsets chosen to frame the face (the Orchestrator should pick exact offsets visually per customer, the same per-customer judgment call `deviceMacroFor`'s own device crops already make; this agent has no image-viewing pass to supply them, flagged honestly rather than guessed). Two stepped crop-window sizes, matching loadout-eva's own BENCH FEED precedent of stepping a fixed 1:1 window rather than fluidly resizing it: `172x172` at WIDE tier, `140x140` at the laptop-tight edge of WIDE (both below the smallest native source, 304px, so both are genuine crops, never upscales). The portrait is INK TINTED to `--r-aux` by default (a dossier photo is 'a different signal class', matching law 1's own gloss), with the same three-treatment FEED-style switch law 5 asks for (see Variations). Empty state (`lethalCustomer === null`, 'nobody yet'): a dashed `--r-struct` bracket-only placeholder sized to the IDENTICAL crop-window footprint (172x172 / 140x140), reusing the existing `kp-piece-hole` dashed-hole idiom scaled up rather than shrunk down, per DAD.LOG's round-3 precedent ('budget equal design attention to the ABSENT case... fixed to the same footprint as the present case'). E. EQUAL-FOOTPRINT RUN STATES (law 4, satisfying the brief's 'no window-height movement between at least two run states' with FOUR states, all sharing one fixed row grid rather than any collapsing block). NO ACTIVE RUN (`run === null`): renders all 6 THIS RUN rows at their normal height with EVERY value replaced by the shipped house placeholder glyph `--` (ASCII double-hyphen, already used identically at report.tsx:406/410 and darknet.tsx:826 for an absent numeric value; never an em or en dash), the CREDITS hero cell showing `--` at full hero scale with its 'cr' unit suppressed, and POUCH/BAYS pip rows rendering fully-unlit pips — NOT the shipped single collapsed 'ACTIVE RUN: none' row (`ledger.tsx:124`), which would make this state shorter than every other and break law 4 outright. DAY 1 OPENER (sparse: runNumber 1, day 1, low stats, no lethal customer, 'MOST USED MODE: none yet' verbatim, BACK ROOM SEALED). MID RUN (dense/healthy: strain > 70 so NEURAL STRAIN reads `--r-ok`, a populated MOST LETHAL cell, BACK ROOM OPEN). DAY 9 STRAINED (dense/risk: strain <= 35, the alarm live, proving C's motion channel against a fully-populated LIFETIME rail). All four states share the identical two-rail-plus-two-focal-cell grid; only cell CONTENT changes, so window height is asserted flat across all four (target ~700px, ceiling 820px, an ESTIMATE pending CDP measurement, see F). F. FLUID RAMP AND WINDOW SIZE. Every size a `clamp()` on `cqi`, one breakpoint at 700px content inline-size, VT323 body floor 19-21px, Silkscreen labels 9-11px, matching law 3 exactly; no `vw` anywhere. Window frame: LEDGER is 'small, table-shaped' per its own law-11 row, narrower than LOADOUT/MANUAL/REPAIR-LOG's WIDE ~860-1150px frames, so this study targets a SINGLE frame width across all three supported viewports rather than a stepped one: `~760px` (reusing loadout-eva's own laptop-tier number, a known-good value that clears the 700px content breakpoint with margin at the tightest supported viewport). This is an ESTIMATE for the Orchestrator to confirm against the CDP harness, not a live measurement (this agent has no browser tool access this cycle). All three supported viewports (16:9 1366x768, 21:9 2560x1080, laptop 1280x800) render the SAME two-column WIDE arrangement; the sub-700px narrow tier (a THIS RUN / LIFETIME tab strip, if it is ever reached) exists only as a tiling fallback, per every other v3 panel's precedent, and no supported viewport reaches it. G. CHOREOGRAPHY. On mount (the shipped component's own framing: 'a fresh statement prints on every open... the window unmounts when closed, so mount = open'): masthead types in first (0-120ms), then the CREDITS hero numeral counts up via loadout-eva's `countUp()` helper reused verbatim, timed to the 6 print-head strikes of the existing `playLedgerPrint()` beat (see H), then THIS RUN's 6 rows slot in staggered (matching the shipped `kp-dotmatrix-print` 4.5ms/dot stagger pattern generalized to rows), then the hazard-stripe divider draws, then LIFETIME's 6 rows slot in staggered, then the MOST LETHAL portrait fades in (a 90ms steps(3) opacity reveal, matching the house pattern for a passive image cell, not a scan-line sweep since this is a filed photo, not a live scan), then the footer dot-matrix prints last exactly as shipped. Every typewriter/count-up is scoped per element (loadout-eva's own established rule) so switching the demo rig's RUN STATE control replays only the affected cells' reveal, not the full mount cascade or a second `playLedgerPrint()` (avoiding sound-spam on rapid rig clicks). Reduced motion: every state renders settled in one frame; `playLedgerPrint()` still fires once, unaffected, matching every sibling panel's rule. H. SOUND: reuse only, zero new presets. `playLedgerPrint()` (audio.ts:320-325: 6x `ledgerTick` at a 32ms stagger with randomized rate, then `ledgerSettle` at 240ms, bus `ui`) already exists, is already tuned to this exact print-head beat, and fires verbatim on every window mount, matching the shipped `useEffect(() => playLedgerPrint(), [])`. Considered and deliberately NOT added: a distinct sound for the NEURAL STRAIN alarm entering the risk band. The desktop's own identical alarm (shop-os.tsx's `STRAIN_ALARM_AT` chip, `ds-riskflash`) is ALREADY silent, motion-and-colour only, so a new sound here would make LEDGER's copy of the same alarm state louder than the original it mirrors, and the alarm is static-on-open rather than a live transition the player watches happen inside this window (unlike REPAIR.LOG's strain TRACE, which animates a live drain). No new interaction exists on this read-only statement beyond the window's own close button, which is already scored elsewhere in the shell. I. TRANSCRIBED CONTENT (verbatim from the current working tree, cited so the Orchestrator can diff against drift): masthead `LEDGER \u2116{meta.runCount}`; BACK ROOM chip value `OPEN`/`SEALED`; strip labels `// THIS RUN _` and `// LIFETIME _`; THIS RUN rows ATTEMPT/`{run.runNumber}`, DAY/`{min(run.day,FINAL_DAY)}/10`, `RAM / TURN`/`{run.ramPerTurn}`, `KIT TIERS`/`S{scanTier} A{attackTier} D{defendTier}`, AUGMENTS/`{run.kit.augments.length}/{boosts}` (boosts=14, AUGMENTS.filter(kind==="boost").length), `NEURAL STRAIN`/`{run.strain}/100` beside the SegMeter; CREDITS cell `{run.credits}` + `cr` unit, POUCH pips (filled=patchPouch.length, total=5), BAYS pips (filled=boostSlots, total=5); LIFETIME rows ATTEMPTS/`{meta.runCount}`, `MACHINE BEATEN`/`{st.runsWon}`, `JOBS CLEARED`/`{st.divesCleared}`, `DIVES LOST`/`{st.divesLost}`, `SCANS RUN`/`{st.scans}`, `MOST USED MODE`/`{MODE_LABEL[mode.key]} x{mode.n}` or `none yet`; MOST LETHAL tag `{lethalCustomer.name.toUpperCase()} x{lethal.n}` or `nobody yet`; footer brand `KP/OS REPAIR BENCH v9.2`. No player-facing string is reworded, shortened, or invented; the only new strings are UX chrome (the `--` empty-state placeholder, already a house idiom, and the `CREDITS`/`POUCH`/`BAYS`/`MOST LETHAL` eyebrows, all already shipped verbatim).

items.idea: Export ONE named constant for the strain risk-alarm threshold from a shared game module (e.g. game/content/kit.ts or game/run-reducer.ts, beside PAR_STRAIN_PER/REDIRECT_STRAIN_PER), and have every window that arms this alarm import it rather than re-declare it. Right now the value 35 is independently hand-typed three times: STRAIN_ALARM_AT = 35 (components/os/shop-os.tsx:67), RISK_BAND = 35 (components/os/windows/report.tsx:58), and an unnamed inline 35/70 pair (components/os/windows/loadout.tsx:328); this cycle's LEDGER v3 spec needed the exact same threshold a fourth time to arm its NEURAL STRAIN alarm consistently with REPAIR.LOG's and the desktop chip's own risk band.
items.why: the four-way agreement on 35 today is coincidental, not guaranteed: a future arc-composer balance pass that moves the risk threshold is a real, foreseeable change, and it would need to find and edit four files by hand. Any one missed copy makes one window's alarm silently disagree with the others about what strain risk means, which is exactly the desync RULINGS.md law 1 is trying to keep impossible ('RISK never shares its colour... appears on exactly one thing per surface') -- that guarantee is only as good as the number every surface reads being the same number.
